item.title: Free agency the new norm? ‘They’re not doing anyone’s contract outside top 15’
item.description: Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC We could see a lot more UFC fighters hitting free agency in the future. It used to be a rarity to see a fighter fight out their contract and enter free agency. The general policy was to see fighters sign a new deal before competing in the final bout on their existing contract. Not any more, according to UFC bantamweight Elijah Smith. Smith came into the UFC through Dana White’s Contender Series and has gone 4-0 with the promotion, three of those ending via finish. He’s not one of those boring decision merchants with no highlights to his name. So it was shocking to hear he wasn’t offered a new contract before fighting out his current contract against Davey Grant last weekend in Las Vegas. And that may be the new norm. “I knew that this was my last fight of my contract, and I was always told that we would probably renew a contract right before the last fight,” Smith told Ariel Helwani. “That didn’t happen. My manager got back to me. He said it’s something that they haven’t done before and they’re not doing anybody’s contract that’s outside of the top 15.” Elijah Smith sheds light on a potential change to the UFC's contract renewal policy: “I'm gonna give it to you guys cutthroat. I'm not gonna sugarcoat anything. I'm gonna tell y'all straight up right here, right now. I knew that this was my last fight of my contract, and I was… pic.twitter.com/WsLPtMSEBt — Ariel Helwani (@arielhelwani) November 10, 2026 “I was surprised,” he continued. “Coming off two finishes, I’m young, I’m marketable, I’m an exciting fighter. Fans want to see me fight. So I was super surprised. From what I’ve heard, that’s not the case in most instances.” “So I don’t know if they want to save money or something or there’s too many people on the roster, but yeah, that’s what it was. I got the fight and they’re not redoing anybody’s contract outside the top 15. So I guess everyone’s just fighting out their contract. I don’t know if that’s for all the weight classes or just the bantamweight weight class, but that’s what was told to me.” For years the UFC has been criticized for being so aggressive when it came to keeping fighters signed to the organization. If you weren’t willing to sign a new contract, there was a good chance you’d end up on the matchmakers’ bad side, potentially affecting your ability to return. That’s no longer the case for those outside the top 15, even firecrackers like Smith. Will this be good for them, or just make things less stable for those starting out their UFC careers?

item.title: Setback for C’River NDC as Deputy Governorship candidate quits, backs Otu
item.description: …governorship candidate expresses shock By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, in Cross River State has suffered a setback ahead of the 2027 governorship election, following the withdrawal of its Deputy Governorship candidate, Mrs. Stella Charles Archibong, from the party’s ticket. Archibong announced her exit in a statement made available to newsmen in Calabar on Wednesday, declaring support for Governor Bassey Otu’s re-election bid under the Back to South Movement. She said her decision followed extensive consultations with elders, family members, the Christian community and political stakeholders across the state. According to her, her responsibility to Cross River was greater than her personal political ambition, hence her resolve to align with the political direction of the Otu administration. “My responsibility to Cross River State is bigger than my individual ambition,” she declared. Archibong also expressed appreciation to the NDC State Chairman, Mr. Goddy Akpama, the party’s governorship candidate, Mr. John Odey, and the national leadership for the opportunity to serve on the party’s platform. She apologised to supporters who might feel disappointed by her decision, and thanked them for their support and confidence throughout her political engagement. Reacting, Odey described her withdrawal as surprising, but urged party members and supporters to remain calm and demonstrate maturity. In a statement, he said the development required calmness, mutual respect and responsible leadership. “This development has come as a surprise. I believe that moments such as this call for calm, maturity, mutual respect, and responsible leadership,” he said. Odey said he held Archibong in high regard and respected her contributions and commitment to the aspirations of Cross River. He disclosed that consultations were ongoing with party leaders, stakeholders and concerned individuals to understand the circumstances surrounding her withdrawal and determine the appropriate next steps. The NDC candidate, however, assured supporters that the party remained committed to building a prosperous, inclusive and economically productive state. The post Setback for C’River NDC as Deputy Governorship candidate quits, backs Otu appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Buhari wanted full military onslaught against N’Delta Avengers, biography reveals
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Late President Muhammadu Buhari’s instinct, when the Niger Delta Avengers began to press the state through sabotage and threat, was to bring “the weight of the armed forces against the insurgents”, an excerpt from his authorised biography has revealed. The account, credited to former Minister of State, Petroleum, Dr Ibe Kachikwu, is contained in “Muhammadu Buhari: The Authorised Biography”, a three-volume work to be publicly presented on Thursday, 19 November 2026, at the Nigerian Army Conference Centre and Suites, Abuja. Chairman of the Planning Committee and former Minister of Water Resources, Engr. Suleiman Adamu announced the presentation at a press conference on Wednesday in Abuja. According to an excerpt od the biography read at the event, “Buhari’s instinct, Kachikwu recalled, was command.” It states: “He felt as a general, he should watch Nigeria, he owed her, and he wanted to act militarily. But Kachikwu argued that a purely military response would create complications. The federal forces were already stretched, escalation could paralyze the entire industry.” The disagreement reached a head ahead of a meeting with the Pan-Niger Delta Forum. “The president was present, and Kachikwu was present,” the book records. “Buhari was upset at what was unfolding in Niger Delta and was very reluctant to approve dialogue with militants.” The excerpt says that, after persuasion, Buhari accepted engagement, “allowing the peace process to proceed.” The excerpt notes that Buhari “was unwilling to tolerate what he regarded as ransom politics, but was nudged into engagement.” It adds that one of Kachikwu’s favourite photographs of the late President was taken just after that meeting, “when he finally smiled because he had been tense.” Kachikwu teased him afterwards. “See, it’s not so bad after all,” Buhari smiled, he said. The author, Dr Udu Yakubu noted that the late President cooperated with the project but did not control its content. “The work was authorised by President Buhari. That authorisation opened doors,” he said, adding: “The subject has had his voice in the biography, while the biographer has had or retained his independence.” The post Buhari wanted full military onslaught against N’Delta Avengers, biography reveals appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Chiefs Facing Tyreek Hill Decision After Josh Downs Trade
item.description: The Kansas City Chiefs were constantly linked to Tyreek Hill ahead of the trade deadline. However, the team traded for Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts instead to bolster its receiving corps. It now faces a decision on the veteran wide receiver. Several analysts and experts considered the position as Kansas City’s “weak spot” and believed it would trade for a wideout. The Chiefs ultimately proved them right by landing Downs in exchange for a fourth- and fifth-round pick. His route running and speed will be a huge weapon for Patrick Mahomes and another target he can maximize. Hill, on the other hand, suffered a gruesome in injury in September 2025 with the Miami Dolphins. He sustained a dislocated left knee and multiple torn ligaments and immediately underwent surgery. The 32-year-old finished last season with 21 receptions for 265 yards and a touchdown. Miami released him last February and remains a free agent. Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Miami Dolphins wide receiver Tyreek Hill (10) practices before the game against the New York Jets at Hard Rock Stadium. Chiefs Could Still Sign Tyreek Hill in the Future Hill’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, revealed on Tuesday that his client is still not medically cleared. However, he expects doctors to give him the green light soon. “On @PatMcAfeeShow, Tyreek Hill’s agent @DrewJRosenhaus said Hill has not been medically cleared yet, but is expected to be medically cleared in a few weeks. Any team that doesn’t land a WR, could be potentially interested in Hill as a free agent as an option,” NFL on Prime’s James Palmer wrote. On @PatMcAfeeShow Tyreek Hill’s agent @DrewJRosenhaus said Hill has not been medically cleared yet, but is expected to be medically cleared in a few weeks. Any team that doesn’t land a WR, could be potentially interested in Hill as a free agent as an option. — James Palmer (@JamesPalmerTV) November 10, 2026 The eight-time Pro Bowler will need to get back to his old conditioning and put in a lot of work before a potential return. He played for the Chiefs from 2016 to 2021 and won one Super Bowl with them. Hill could be a game changer if he can get his peak form back. However, it’s easier said than done especially coming from a major surgery. Downs is also younger than him and hasn’t reached his peak yet. But Hill shouldn’t be counted out completely. He has the experience, as well as familiarity playing with Patrick Mahomes and Kansas City’s other veterans. item.title: Gabriel Magalhaes defends Barcelona star Raphinha over Brazil statements: ‘Many misinterpreted what he said’
item.description: Gabriel Magalhaes defends Barcelona star Raphinha over Brazil statements: ‘Many misinterpreted what he said’ Arsenal defender Gabriel Magalhaes has publicly defended Barcelona winger Raphinha following criticism of his recent comments about managing his playing time with the Brazilian national team. Speaking at a press conference in Singapore on Wednesday, the centre-back insisted that his teammate’s words had been misunderstood and emphasised his commitment to representing Brazil. Raphinha attracted criticism after explaining that Carlo Ancelotti understood the need to manage his minutes because he was still recovering from an injury. The Barcelona forward had stressed that he was not yet fully fit and wanted the national team coach to take his physical condition into consideration. “The national team coach will know how to manage my playing time. We’ve spoken, and he knows I’m not yet at 100% fitness. “I ask Barcelona fans not to worry about this,” said Raphinha during his contract renewal ceremony. Gabriel Magalhaes insists Raphinha was misunderstood Raphinha was criticised for his statement on national team coach Carlo Ancelotti. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) Gabriel, who also has experience dealing with injuries during international duty, believes the reaction to Raphinha’s comments was misplaced. The Arsenal defender explained that professional footballers cannot always maintain the same physical and mental intensity throughout a demanding calendar. “We are high-level players, and what we always want is to play. I think many misinterpreted what Raphinha said. We are human, and sometimes we need to rest, even mentally. “In Europe, we play every two or three days, and there are many matches. “When we join the national team, we want to make the most of our time here and learn, but many misinterpret some statements, and that’s what happened with Raphinha,” he explained. Brazil dressing room backs Barcelona winger Gabriel Magalhaes has defended Raphinha. (Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images) Gabriel also made it clear that Raphinha’s comments had not created any concern within the Brazilian dressing room. Instead, he highlighted the Barcelona forward’s dedication and importance to the national team. “Within the group, we didn’t understand his words to mean that he came here to rest or anything like that. “We know his dedication to the national team well; his commitment is exemplary, and he is an ideal player for us.” The discussion comes as Brazil prepare for two friendlies in Singapore , facing Japan on November 14 before meeting the hosts three days later. Source: Mundo Deportivo

item.title: Senate summons NCC, MTN, others over dropped calls, airtime deductions
item.description: By Henry Umoru, Abuja The Senate has summoned the Nigerian Communications Commission, NCC, and telecommunications operators, including MTN, Airtel, Globacom and T2, over persistent dropped calls, failed connections and unexplained airtime deductions suffered by subscribers. The NCC and telecommunication operators are expected to appear before Senator Aliyu Ikra Bilbis, Zamfara Central-led Senate Committee on Communications. The Committee was mandated to invite the Nigerian Communications Commission and telecommunications operators to investigate complaints of airtime deductions for failed calls, dropped calls, prematurely terminated conversations and inflated charges. The committee is also expected to establish the financial losses suffered by subscribers and report back to the Senate within four weeks, with recommendations for further legislative and regulatory action. The resolution of the Senate on Wednesday was a sequel to a motion titled “Need to curb unjustified deductions from subscribers’ airtime resulting from substandard telecommunications services through robust consumer protection.” The motion was sponsored by the Senate Chief Whip, Senator Mohammed Tahir Monguno, APC, Borno North. Senator Ned Nwoko, APC, Delta North, who seconded the motion, described the proposal as a straightforward consumer-protection intervention, insisting that the problem affects virtually every Nigerian who relies on telecommunications services. He lamented the contrast between the quality of telephone services in Nigeria and the seamless connectivity experienced in other countries. Presenting the motion on behalf of Monguno, the Deputy Majority Leader, Senator Lola Ashiru, APC, Kwara South, expressed concerns over consumers being charged for calls that were never successfully completed, with lawmakers demanding accountability, refunds and improved quality of service across the telecommunications industry. According to the Senate, for millions of Nigerians, making a telephone call has increasingly become an expensive gamble, just as poor network connectivity, dropped calls, interrupted conversations and failed connections have become recurring complaints among subscribers, many of whom lose airtime even when calls are not successfully completed. Senators warned that Nigerians should not be made to pay for telecommunications services that have not been effectively delivered. They noted that subscribers are frequently compelled to redial numbers several times before establishing a connection, resulting in additional airtime deductions and financial losses, particularly for low-income earners, traders, students and small business owners. The Senate argued that while network challenges may sometimes be unavoidable, consumers should not bear the financial consequences of service failures beyond their control. item.title: 'My captain Shreyas, my coach Ricky': Hardik Pandya's first comment after joining Punjab Kings
item.description: NEW DELHI: Hardik Pandya has made his first public comment after joining Punjab Kings (PBKS) ahead of the 2027 IPL season. Pandya has moved from Mumbai Indians (MI) to Punjab Kings for Rs 18 crore. In return, PBKS have traded fast bowler Arshdeep Singh to MI. The trade has been completed ahead of the 2027 IPL season. Pandya's new fee of Rs 18 crore is higher than his earlier fee of Rs 16.35 crore. Arshdeep has moved to MI at his existing fee of Rs 18 crore, according to an IPL statement. The all-rounder shared a message on Instagram, mentioning his new captain Shreyas Iyer, coach Ricky Ponting and the team. "Sat Sri Akal. My Captain. Shreyas. My Coach. Ricky. My team. All of Punjab. I am standing behind you," Pandya wrote. The move brings an end to Pandya's second stint with Mumbai Indians, where he won four IPL titles. Pandya first joined MI in 2015 and played a key role in their title-winning campaigns in 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2020. He returned to the franchise in 2024 and took over as captain from Rohit Sharma. However, MI struggled during this period. 135731411 In 162 IPL matches, Pandya has scored 2,955 runs at a strike rate of 146.28 and taken 82 wickets. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Hardik Pandya (@hardikpandya93) Arshdeep moves to Mumbai Indians Arshdeep, meanwhile, joins MI after spending eight seasons with Punjab Kings. He made his IPL debut for PBKS in 2019 and became one of the leading left-arm fast bowlers in the competition. He has taken 111 wickets in 96 IPL matches and is Punjab Kings' all-time leading wicket-taker.

item.title: "I might have deserved the opportunity a little more" – Ter Stegen opens up on rivalry with Neuer
item.description: "I might have deserved the opportunity a little more" – Ter Stegen opens up on rivalry with Neuer Heading into Germany's upcoming games against Serbia and the Netherlands, Marc-André ter Stegen has been named as Jürgen Klopp undisputed first choice in goal. For the 34-year-old, this marks a welcome change after years of playing second fiddle to Manuel Neuer and struggling with injuries. In an interview with Sport Bild, ter Stegen looks back on his long-standing rivalry with the now 40-year-old Bayern Munich shot-stopper, who announced his international retirement for good after last summer's World Cup. While ter Stegen clearly has huge respect for Neuer's qualities, he makes no secret of the fact that he would have liked to play more than the 45 games he has featured in for Germany at senior level. “Manuel Neuer is not simply a great goalkeeper. We don't need to fool ourselves about that: he is probably one of the best goalkeepers of all time. He also had an enormous standing within the national team, and rightly so. However, he was also held back by injuries,” ter Stegen said. “And who knows more about that than I do, unfortunately? Nevertheless, I believe a certain level of competition pushes the goalkeeper who gets to play to improve. That's how it was with us. “Even so, the question naturally remains: would I rather have been playing? Of course! But the coaches we had with the national team chose Manu. You have to respect that, and I have to accept it. That's simply part of sport.” The 34-year-old did admit that there were times when he felt he deserved to play ahead of Neuer, despite not being given the opportunity. “Did I sometimes have to bite my tongue? Did I sometimes swear under my breath when nobody was listening? Certainly! There were also moments when I felt I might have deserved the opportunity a little more,” he said. One particularly bitter moment for ter Stegen came at the 2018 World Cup, when Neuer managed to return from a long-term injury and reclaim his place in the starting line-up ahead of him despite lacking match practice. “That was the most bitter moment, but I don't want to revisit it. The fact remains that the coach (Jogi Löw at the time, ed.) makes the decision. You can get as angry as you like,” said ter Stegen, who is currently Ajax's first-choice goalkeeper while on loan from FC Barcelona.

item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. Because we didn’t create success for our team this season.” Latest Ducks news Oregon makes a big leap in latest College Football Playoff rankings Dan Lanning backs expanded college football playoff to 24 teams Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham takes shot at Oregon’s $50M roster Read the original article on oregonlive.com . item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday. item.title: Chad Tracy finishes third in AL Manager of the Year race
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, FL - SEPTEMBER 27: Manager Chad Tracy #17 of the Boston Red Sox looks on from the dugout prior to the game between the Chicago Cubs and the Boston Red Sox at Tropicana Field on Sunday, September 27, 2026 in St. Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Scott Audette/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images Is Manager of the Year the dumbest award in baseball? I think it is. For starters, no one cares about it. I mean no one. Can you name a single winner of the Manager of the Year Award of the past 10 years? Don’t even think about lying to me, you obviously cannot. And that’s a good thing. Baseball is a player’s game. This isn’t college hoops, where the ego-puffing men performatively screaming on the sideline are bigger stars than the players themselves. Baseball managers aren’t stars at all. They’re just kind of there. To belabor the sky metaphor, baseball managers are clouds, at best. And because baseball is a player’s game — one that’s decided on the field instead of in the pages of a playbook — almost no one on the outside is even capable of evaluating the job a manager does. Managers don’t have elaborate styles of play they bring from one team to another. They don’t spend days designing defensive schemes that befuddle more talented teams. Their job is mostly to keep the clubhouse happy and pull a pitcher at the right moment. That’s just about it. And because the job is so hard to evaluate from the outside, voting usually follows a predictable pattern: voters just give it to the manager of the team that had a better season than anyone expected. They do this despite the fact that we all know that, every single season, there will be flukey teams who get a little magic fairy dust sprinkled on them and make a surprising playoff run. That’s just how baseball works and, more often than not, those teams go right on back to being mediocre-to-bad the next season. So, e.g., we give the 2023 NL Manager of the Year to Skip Schumaker. After all, the 2022 Marlins only won 69 games, so Schumaker guiding the same team to 84 wins the next season obviously means he did an amazing job, right? Of course — just please try to ignore the fact that he must have forgotten how to manage the next year, because the same team with the same manager subsequently went 62-100 the very next season. All of this is to say: I don’t really care that Chad Tracy didn’t win the American League Manager of the Year last night. He finished third, behind winner Will Venable of the White Sox and runner-up Kevin Cash of the Rays. Did either Venable or Cash truly do a better job than Tracy? No one knows. What they do know is that the Red Sox were predicted to make the playoffs before the season started, while the White Sox and Rays were not. Ergo, those managers must have done a great job. item.title: The Promise And The Proof
item.description: Tinubu is asking for time to complete his reforms. His challengers must explain how they would deliver better results. The most consequential promise from today’s campaign platform concerns something Nigerians can judge without a political analyst: whether the lights stay on. Speaking at the APC rally in Dutse, President Bola Tinubu promised reliable electricity, lower living costs, support for smaller businesses and more jobs if re-elected. These commitments reach directly into the daily calculations of households and enterprises. For the tailor buying fuel, the graduate searching for work and the family stretching its food budget, the question is immediate: how soon will improvement arrive? That question now sits at the centre of Tinubu’s re-election argument. The APC unveiled its second-term manifesto today, defending the administration’s reforms while promising improvements in security, living standards, infrastructure and governance. The campaign is asking Nigerians to connect the disruption of the present with the prospect of a more prosperous future. It is a politically demanding request. Voters must decide whether the government has established a credible foundation for improvement and whether their experience gives them sufficient reason to renew its mandate. A New Manifesto Meets An Existing Record An incumbent’s manifesto arrives with a companion document: the record of the government seeking another term. The APC’s new commitments include additional electricity meters, wider health insurance coverage and a reduction in the number of out-of-school children. Its presentation also promised identifiable delivery responsibilities and public reporting of progress. These are campaign commitments, whose implementation remains to be demonstrated. That creates an opportunity for a more useful election debate. On electricity, candidates should explain how proposed investments would improve supply to homes and businesses. On employment, they should distinguish training places, temporary opportunities and sustained paid work. On education, they should explain how children will enter school, remain there and learn. The opposition has a responsibility here too. Criticism of government performance becomes more persuasive when accompanied by a workable alternative. A promise to make life affordable needs an explanation of costs, funding and consequences. A promise to improve security needs an account of personnel, intelligence, accountability and protection for affected communities. The campaign can now be judged against specific proposals. Nigerians should expect the candidates to defend them. item.title: Tinubu seeks Reps’ approval for $7.7bn external borrowing plan in 2026 budget
item.description: By GiftChapiOdekina, Abuja President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has written to the House of Representatives, seeking legislative approval for the implementation of the N10.79 trillion ($7.7 billion) external borrowing component of the 2026 Appropriation Act. The request, contained in a letter addressed to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, seeks approval to raise $7.707 billion at the budget exchange rate of N1,400 to the dollar to finance part of the Federal Government’s budget deficit. However, the President clarified that the request does not constitute a fresh borrowing plan, explaining that the National Assembly had already approved the amount and made provision for it in the 2026 Appropriation Act. According to him, the current request is aimed at fulfilling the statutory requirements of Sections 21(1) and 27(1) of the Debt Management Office (DMO) Establishment Act, 2003, which require parliamentary approval of the terms and conditions governing external loans. Tinubu explained that Section 21(1) prohibits the Minister of Finance from obtaining or approving external loans unless their terms and conditions have been presented to and approved by the National Assembly. He added that Section 27(1) empowers the National Assembly to approve standard terms and conditions for negotiating and accepting external loans and issuing guarantees. The President recalled that the 2026 Appropriation Act provided for N29.218 trillion in new borrowings to finance the budget deficit, comprising N18.28 trillion in domestic borrowing and N10.79 trillion in external borrowing. He said the Federal Government would pursue multiple financing options simultaneously, taking into consideration their costs, benefits and the time required to access the funds. Tinubu, however, indicated that greater emphasis would be placed on Eurobond issuance, which he said could be concluded more quickly and provide access to larger amounts of financing at relatively lower costs. On the proposed Eurobond issuance, the President noted that the final terms and conditions would be determined at the time of pricing, depending on prevailing market conditions. He assured that the Federal Ministry of Finance and the Debt Management Office would work to secure the most favourable terms available in the international market. According to the letter, the external borrowing is intended to finance projects and programmes captured in the 2026 budget, particularly in priority sectors including defence and security, transportation, agriculture, power, education and health. Tinubu said the borrowing would also support the administration’s efforts to stabilise and strengthen ongoing macroeconomic reforms. He further argued that the proceeds would contribute to the country’s external reserves, as the funds would be received by the Central Bank of Nigeria on behalf of the Federal Government, thereby supporting the naira exchange rate. item.title: Joe Lacob talks Juste Jocyte’s future after Natalie Nakase drama
item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Golden State Valkyries owner Joe Lacob isn’t shutting the door on Juste Jocyte. Juste Jocyte didn’t bite her tongue after spending basically the entire WNBA Finals glued to the pine, seeing just six total minutes on the floor. The 20-year-old made her feelings known in an interview with the Lithuanian media, making it clear she was miserable with how Natalie Nakase used her. Now, heading into the offseason, Jocyte is putting the Valkyries front office on notice, telling them she has zero interest in riding the bench next year, and she won’t stick around without real minutes. Joe Lacob issues an update on Juste Jocyte’s future Joe Lacob is trying to play damage control before the situation spirals. Instead of taking the bait and firing back at Jocyte’s comments, the Valkyries owner is playing the long game, making it clear he doesn’t want to let the 20-year-old walk away. He said: “I kind of understand she’s competitive and would like to win and didn’t play. But she’s also only 20. We had a pretty great roster, very deep. I think she can be a very good player and we’d really love to have her back. “So I think she will certainly earn a lot more playing time in the future. She didn’t get to play as much as she wanted to, and that’s understandable. “I think she can be a very good player and we would really love to have her back.” Even with Lacob trying to play nice, it’s hard to picture Jocyte sticking around in the Bay. That bridge with Nakase is burned, and Golden State isn’t about to let locker room bad blood poison the culture they’re building. Once trust is shot, a clean break is the only realistic way out. item.title: Jake Paul doubles down on retirement claims with 100% certainty if he loses to Cedric Doumbe
item.description: Jake Paul doubles down on retirement claims with 100% certainty if he loses to Cedric Doumbe appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After almost a year long absence from boxing, celebrity boxer Jake Paul is now finally coming back. Set to box French kickboxer Cedric Doumbe in Dubai on Dec. 24, 2026, Paul had recently promised to retire if he lost to Doumbe. Paul broke his jaw last year during his fight against Anthony Joshua and has now been cleared to come back. Ahead of the fight, Paul uploaded a video on his social media, where he said, “If he wins, I will hang up the gloves and call it a day,” Paul said. “But if he loses, the man who calls himself ‘The Best’ just got beat up by a YouTuber with a titanium jaw. So, Cedric Doumbe—I, Jake Joseph Paul, will knock you out, embarrass you, and defeat you on Christmas Eve.” (via ESPN) Now, days later, at the Paul-Doumbe fight press conference in Paris, France, “The Problem Child” doubled down on his retirement claims . “100% retiring if I lose to this guy. Sure, like 100%. For sure.For sure, for sure,” Paul said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Despite his retirement claims, Paul also managed to fit in a subtle compliment for the veteran Kickboxer. “We’re ready for this guy. Kickboxing world champion, ‌Glory champion, one of the best in MMA. This guy’s great. He is great. Very bien. But he’s getting knocked the f*** out on Christmas Eve,” Paul said at the press conference. “Kickboxing will not help him, people. On December 24th, the legs will just be used for transportation. ​This is boxing. He’s gonna learn a very, very hard lesson. And at the end of the day, he’s ​still a tune-up fight for me.” While Paul has wins over several iconic fighters, Doumbe comes with a unique moveset and challenge of his own . Doumbe, 34, transitioned from a kickboxing career (63-7-1) to MMA, and had his last boxing match in 2015. item.title: Dodgers to meet with Tarik Skubal
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 11: Tarik Skubal #29 of the Los Angeles Dodgers throws a pitch against the Milwaukee Brewers during the second inning in game one of the National League Championship Series at American Family Field on October 11, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The race for the Tarik Skubal sweepstakes has begun, and the Dodgers are once again in the mix for the best free agent talent on the market. While the left-hander will be stripped of his title as the reigning two-time American League Cy Young winner over the coming days, he is the ultimate envy of any team that can afford his services. In their pursuit of re-signing the team’s Game 1 starter of the postseason, the Dodgers will be meeting with Skubal, yet the details surrounding when and where the meeting will take place have yet to be disclosed, notes Sonja Chen of MLB.com . “We’ve been in touch with his camp, and our expectation is we’ll meet at some point,” [Brandon] Gomes told reporters, including MLB.com’s Anthony Castrovince, at the GM Meetings in Las Vegas. The Dodgers are competing with teams such as the New York Mets, Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres in the hunt for Skubal, and the Mets have already scheduled a meeting with Skubal for next week, per Jorge Castillo of ESPN . Castillo notes that Mets president of baseball operations David Stearns declined to comment on their pursuit of Skubal. LAS VEGAS — The New York Mets are scheduled to meet with left-handed pitcher Tarik Skubal, the prize of this offseason’s free agent class, next week in California, a source confirmed to ESPN on Tuesday. No player in the history of Major League Baseball has been handed a nine-figure salary for one year of service, but Dylan Hernandez of the California Post makes an outlandish proposal for the Dodgers to offer Skubal a one-year deal for $100 million. They will have to offer Skubal enough money to forfeit the security of a longer deal. What about $100 million to pitch for them next year? Perhaps a player option or two after that? If nine figures for one season of baseball sounds expensive, consider the cost of not retaining Skubal. Former Dodgers shortstop and 2020 World Series MVP Corey Seager could be finding greener pastures for 2027 and beyond, as Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic reports that the Texas Rangers intend on trading Seager this offseason. The Rangers, though, intend to explore moving Seager at the general managers’ meetings, according to people briefed on their intentions who spoke on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly.

item.title: No. 1 junior Asterisk Talley not signing with Stanford but remains committed
item.description: The top-ranked female golfer in the Class of 2027 won’t be signing during the week-long early signing period, which began Wednesday. While Stanford will sign another highly ranked recruit in Anna Fang, the Cardinal will hold off in adding No. 1 junior Asterisk Talley, the reigning U.S. Women’s Amateur champion who is ranked fourth in the World Amateur Golf Ranking. The 17-year-old Talley, who hails from Chowchilla, California, remains verbally committed to Stanford and can sign at any point, but Talley is also undecided about her future as she chases an LPGA card through the tour’s Elite Amateur Pathway. “It’s still definitely in conversation,” Talley said of playing college golf. “It’s definitely an undecided still, but I think it’s something to think about over the next few months, and it’s definitely going to be an interesting path to kind of take. Both have their upsides and their cons, too. It’s definitely going to be a go-with-the-flow kind of thing and see what happens in these coming months.” Due to NCAA rules, Stanford head coach Anne Walker cannot comment on prospective student-athletes like Talley, though she'll soon officially welcome Fang, Golf Channel’s No. 2 junior in the class behind only Wake Forest signee Amelie Zalsman, to her program. Signing Day: Ranking top classes, players for Class of 2027 Most years, the No. 1 recruit in NCAA men’s golf is up for discussion. This year, there is no debate as Miles Russell, arguably the best prospect in over a decade, signs with Florida State. Brentley Romine , Brentley Romine , Talley isn’t the first No. 1 women’s recruit not to sign during the early signing period; Yuka Saso was verbally committed to Georgia for the Class of 2020, but she never put pen to paper for the Bulldogs, instead turning professional later that November. While the launch of Talley's pro career isn't expected to be as imminent, she currently sits at 15 LEAP points and has plenty of opportunities to get to 20 and earn LPGA status. She is already exempt into four major championships next year, starting with the Chevron Championship in April. Made cuts in majors award one point while top-25s come with as additional point. Non-major LPGA events hand out one point for a top-40 or two points for a top-10. Talley can also earn two more points via the WAGR, one for reaching No. 3 and another for getting to No. 1. She’ll also have the chance this spring to win the Augusta National Women’s Amateur, a title that comes with two points. If Talley were to reach 20 points before July 1, 2027, it’s likely she’d still wait until that date to turn pro and take up LPGA membership as that would afford her essentially a season and a half on the LPGA compared to just the remainder of the current season should she make the jump before July 1. “Getting out there early is always an advantage. … You only have so much time,” Talley added. “But there’s always room to grow in college and get that extra experience with the team; it’s something y

item.title: MCC to introduce Spirit of Cricket Award at ILT20 Season 5
item.description: The Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) will introduce a Spirit of Cricket Award at the ILT20 Season 5, recognising a team or individual who best reflects the game's values during the tournament, which begins in the UAE on November 21. The award will be presented at the end of the competition on December 20, marking the first such recognition at the six-team T20 league. MCC, the guardian of cricket's Laws, will work with the tournament organisers to promote sportsmanship and fair play among players. The partnership is part of MCC's wider effort to promote the Spirit of Cricket across the game. The Club has previously worked with ICC Europe to present similar awards at three men's sub-regional World Cup qualification events earlier this year. Rob Lynch, MCC's Director of Cricket and Operations, said franchise leagues could play an important role in setting standards for player behaviour. “MCC sees franchise leagues as the standard-bearers for playing the game in the right way – playing hard but playing fair and with a smile on your face,” Lynch said. He added that the competitive nature of franchise cricket, where international team-mates often face each other, could help improve conduct across the sport. Mike Fordham, Interim Chief Operating Officer of the ILT20, said the partnership aligned with the league's emphasis on sporting values. He also pointed to the participation of players from 19 cricketing nations across its six franchises this season. “The tournament has always been hugely competitive with top quality cricket on display. Our matches have always been played in the right spirit with cricket’s traditional sporting values remaining at the forefront,” Fordham said. Season 5 will run from November 21 to December 20, with matches scheduled at the Sheikh Zayed Cricket Stadium in Abu Dhabi, Dubai International Stadium and Sharjah Cricket Stadium. Defending champions Desert Vipers will be joined by Gulf Giants, MI Emirates, Dubai Capitals, Abu Dhabi Knight Riders and Sharjah Warriorz in the 34-match competition. Previous winners include Gulf Giants, MI Emirates and Dubai Capitals. The new recognition will be separate from the main MCC Spirit of Cricket Award, established by MCC and the BBC in 2013 in honour of Christopher Martin-Jenkins.

item.description: I have written a couple of articles regarding the bad bullpen of 2026, one focused on how good bullpens really do have a lot of correlation to winning teams, and the other about how the 2026 bullpen was one of the worst 21st century Cardinals bullpens. Now I would like to look at some options in free agency that St Louis could possibly go after in order to bolster the bad bullpen. Aware that it is quite possible that the Cardinals will do absolutely nothing this offseason when it comes to free agency, I still think they should spend a little bit to stabilize the bullpen issue. The Cardinals rarely let their bullpen stink for long, so maybe they’ll actually sign a guy or two. There are many options on the market this offseason when it comes to relievers! If a reliever seems just really bad and not an option, I won’t mention them. I will however mention good options we probably won’t afford. The ugly FIPs make him look like replacement level fodder, but maybe there’s something there for the Cardinals. He might not be too expensive. While he’s always been an overperformer on FIP, there may be some concern about his 2026 season, as his FIP rates went even higher than usual. Still, his ERA works for me, and the xERA isn’t alarming. He is pretty old, however! item.title: Jason Brown, having weathered the storm, brings his figure skating career back home
item.description: It was noon Friday, and the Blackhawks Ice Center just west of downtown Chicago was teeming with teenage hockey players and their equipment. Three of the center’s four ice surfaces were in use for a weekend hockey tournament. The fourth rink, where Jason Brown was headed, would be filled with 16 figure skaters of various ages and skill levels, from the abilities that have made the 31-year-old Brown a two-time Olympian to those of tiny 8-year-olds trying to master a waltz jump. Brown folded up the workout mat he had squeezed into one unoccupied space in a lobby behind one of the rinks. He put the devices used to stretch and warm up back into a small roller suitcase, laced his skates and walked over to the fourth rink, where an open freestyle session was beginning. 2026 Saatva Skate America: How to watch, schedule, preview of figure skating Grand Prix Skate America, the biggest annual international figure skating event in the U.S., airs live on NBC Sports and Peacock. Nick Zaccardi , For the next hour, he would run through the programs to be unveiled this week at Saatva Skate America, work on individual jumps and try to avoid running into one of the younger skaters weaving across the ice, blissfully unaware of just how fast Brown can move. At one point, his coach/choreographer, Rohene Ward, would need to motion emphatically to shoo a skater from a spot in the line of Brown’s backward takeoff for a triple Lutz jump. The experience of dodging other skaters was more uplifting than annoying to Brown. It took him back 20 years or so, to when he was living at the family home in Highland Park, 25 miles to the north, and training at Chicago area rinks where workouts also were not divided by skill level. “I grew up with that,” Brown said. “To see those kids out there in their own world is pure joy.” Joy from skating had been in short supply for Brown in the several months after a startlingly poor free skate at January’s Prevagen U.S. Championships ,which he unhesitatingly calls “disastrous.” It included two falls, three popped jumps and just one clean triple jump, and it received a score that was his lowest in 13 seasons. He had been third despite a lightly flawed short program but dropped to eighth overall. Brown actually could see it coming. And yet it still caught him unprepared. After all, if there had been one thing constant about Brown’s lengthy career as a senior skater, it was his consistency, especially at major events. In an era when quadruple jumps became the coin of the realm, the quad-less Brown had still cashed in: a gold medal, four silvers and three bronzes at nationals since 2014; and three top-eight finishes at the World Championships that helped the U.S. to get the full allocation of three men’s singles spots at the Olympics the next season. Two of the three times, in 2018 and 2026, he didn’t get one of the Olympic spots he helped earn. item.title: Chelsea right-back Malo Gusto open to January transfer
item.description: Chelsea right-back Malo Gusto open to January transfer Chelsea right-back Malo Gusto (23) is open to leaving Chelsea in the January transfer window, according to the BBC . The France international is far from being a guaranteed starter in West London. Since Xabi Alonso’s appointment at Chelsea FC, Gusto’s playign time has dramatically decreased. Despite Reece James’ injury, the former Olympique Lyonnais Academy graduate only started three Premier League games, the last of which dating back to two months ago. The BBC reports that Gusto is set to assess his options before the January transfer window, as he lost his place to Josh Acheampong at right-back. Chelsea were reportedly open to selling the France international right-back – currently at Clairefontaine with Zinédine Zidane’s squad – in exchange for a €85m transfer fee. The player reportedly agreed to join Manchester City at the time , where he would have reunited with former Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca. Gusto featured 100 times for Chelsea since signing a seven-and-a-half year deal in January 2023. GFFN | Bastien Cheval

item.title: Drew Rosenhaus shares what he thinks will happen if San Francisco 49ers release Brandon Aiyuk
item.description: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images Brandon Aiyuk officially made his return to the San Francisco 49ers last Friday, and his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, believes the player could either return to the team or be moved as a free agent. The wide receiver was at loggerheads with the franchise and called out coach Kyle Shanahan and members of the front office. However, after approaching the league, he was reinstated, and this means the 49ers now have two weeks to decide what they want to do with him. Aiyuk last played for the 49ers in October 2024 and has since been out due to an injury. After being reinstated, he has passed his physical examination, but the 49ers have already made the decision to move on from him. His agent, Drew Rosenhaus, is confident that won’t change Aiyuk’s plans for the rest of the season. “Brandon will either play for the 49ers when the two weeks are up, or they can decide to release him, in which case he will be a free agent. And I expect that there will be interest in him. I definitely expect him to play this season. Judging by the comments from coach Shanahan, it doesn’t sound like they plan on bringing Brandon back. So, when the two weeks are over, it’s my job to potentially find a new team for him. And I’m confident now that he’s healthy, he will play,” said Rosenhaus on The Pat McAfee Show. All offseason, Aiyuk was pushing for a move to the Washington Commanders to team up with Jayden Daniels, who was his teammate at Arizona State University. However, things got a little complicated when Aiyuk then called out Daniels, leading to the QB even unfollowing the 49ers player. Before his injury, Aiyuk was one of the best WRs in the league and even made the Second Team All-Pro. His antics have definitely made it difficult for teams to trust him, but if a franchise is willing to take a chance, this could prove to be a high-risk, high-reward move. item.title: Robert Horry Rips Walker Kessler’s Offensive Game: “Guys In Elementary Got Better Post Moves Than Him”
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers have the NBA’s best record at 10-2, and new arrival Walker Kessler has played his part in their early success. Kessler has impressed on defense, and former Laker Robert Horry likes what he has seen from the big man on that end of the floor. What Horry, who won three titles with the Lakers, doesn’t like, though, is Kessler’s offensive game, and he urged him to improve on the Big Shot Bob Podcast . “You know what’s really scary about Walker Kessler?” Horry said. “Hey, I know guys in elementary got better post moves than him. He got no post moves, man. I’m like, who is teaching this dude any post moves? You’re seven f***ing feet tall. Get you a little jump hook, man. You don’t have to dunk everything.” Kessler really doesn’t have a reliable post move. The 25-year-old is primarily a rim-runner, and if you are good at that next to Luka Doncic , you’ll score some points. Kessler is averaging 14.9 points, 10.8 rebounds, 1.7 assists, 1.3 steals, and 2.3 blocks per game for the Lakers in 2026-27. Over 60 percent of his field goal attempts have been within three feet of the basket, and only 1.8 percent have come from beyond 10 feet. Now, Kessler showed off some range in the 2025-26 season for the Utah Jazz . He went 6-8 from three in five games before needing season-ending shoulder surgery. So, when the Lakers acquired Kessler, the No. 22 pick in the 2022 NBA Draft, from the Jazz in the summer, the expectation was that he’d be a threat from beyond the arc. He even shared that head coach JJ Redick wanted him to shoot more threes , but he hasn’t even attempted a single one through 12 games. “I don’t even think he wants to score ’cause I’ve seen him get offensive rebounds and kick that b***h out instead of crunching that b***h,” Horry said. “… I’m like, dude, you 7 ft tall. Get you a power dribble. Go up and dunk that b***h too. Like [Shaquille O’Neal], you monkey dunk that b***h. That’s what he said. That’s what Shaq used to say. So dunk on somebody and then just move on. “That’s what I want him to do and stop kicking that b***h out ’cause you don’t get no plays ran for you,” Horry added. Now, teams like the player who gets the offensive rebound to kick it out for an open three. That could well be the case here, but we don’t know for sure. While Kessler isn’t the perfect offensive center, that wasn’t why the Lakers gave him a four-year, $130 million contract and gave up two first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps to the Jazz. They wanted a rim runner and a defensive anchor, and he is just that. “He’s a great shot blocker,” Horry said. “And the thing I like about Kessler the best is he goes after everything. And even though he’s gotten dunked on a couple times, he don’t give a s***… He’s still going to go out and try to block. That’s what I like about real, true shot blockers.” Only Victor Wembanyama (4.4) and Myles Turner (2.4) are averaging more blocks per game than Kessler this seas

item.title: Top 2027 recruit Amaya Manuel commits to Tennessee
item.description: Top 2027 recruit Amaya Manuel has committed to Tennessee , she announced. The 5-8 point guard from Saint Louis (MO) Lift For Life Academy chose the Lady Vols over programs including Missouri and Arkansas. “Definitely a family type of environment,” she previously told Rivals of factors she was considering. “I want to do a lot of team bonding and stuff. I really want to have a good relationship with all the teammates and all my coaches. I also want a program that’s big on development for each player. You know, let me do what I what I can do, not limiting me, but making me better.” Tennessee earned the last official visit and the commitment. The Lady Vols are getting a strong point guard in Manuel. “My biggest strength is definitely driving,” she said. “I just came back from my ACL injury in November, so I’m just now coming back, but I’ve always been able to drive and be aggressive. I’m trying to get back to that. I still think that’s my strength, but I need to get better at that now.” Manuel marks Tennessee’s second commitment in the 2027 class after adding versatile wing Maci Pringle.

item.title: JJ Gabriel set to sign Real Madrid contract by early next week – report
item.description: JJ Gabriel set to sign Real Madrid contract by early next week – report Real Madrid are expected to complete the signing of Manchester United youngster JJ Gabriel by the beginning of next week, with the 16-year-old’s move to the Spanish capital approaching its final stages. According to journalist Ben Fernandes Santos , the agreement is close to being finalised, with the teenager having made his preference clear to the European clubs interested in securing his signature. It is to be noted that Gabriel attracted attention across Europe following his decision to leave Manchester United in September. Real Madrid, after tough negotiations and a fight with other suitors, emerged as his preferred destination, with Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain among the clubs previously linked with the highly-rated forward. Manchester United fail to convince JJ Gabriel to stay Manchester United reportedly made several attempts to change Gabriel’s mind, with club executives and manager Michael Carrick holding discussions with the player and his representatives. Real Madrid could announce JJ Gabriel’s signing by next week. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images) However, those efforts did not alter his intention to pursue a move to Real Madrid. The teenager requested to leave United in September and has since been training independently in Spain while his future is being resolved. His decision became clearer when he was asked to choose between Barcelona and Real Madrid . “Obviously, Real Madrid,” he said. As reported before, Real Madrid had reached a verbal agreement with the teenager and were confident of signing him. However, formal club-to-club negotiations had not yet taken place until a few weeks back. Real Madrid have a clear development plan Real Madrid have won the race for JJ Gabriel. (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images) Real Madrid are understood to want Gabriel to begin his development with Castilla , allowing him to experience senior football while remaining close to the first-team environment. The Spanish club believe their pathway offers an attractive opportunity for the teenager to progress towards the senior squad. His representative, Ali Barat, has been involved in discussions over the move, while reports have also suggested that Jose Mourinho played a role in convincing Gabriel that Madrid would be the right destination. All in all, Real Madrid are set to sign the highly-rated teenager, and the official announcement could be arriving soon.

item.title: UGA Takes Top Spot As CFP Rankings Face Upheaval
item.description: Nov 7, 2026; Oxford, Mississippi, USA; Georgia Bulldogs wide receiver Talyn Taylor (1) celebrates with tight end Ethan Barbour (9) after scoring a touchdown against the Mississippi Rebels during the second half at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images The College Football Playoff selection committee released its second rankings on Tuesday night , placing Georgia at No. 1 after their dominant 42-7 win over Ole Miss. The top spot changed hands, while Miami dropped six places to No. 7 despite losing by only a touchdown. This week’s list shows massive movement across the board, with no team staying in the same position as last week. Georgia, Notre Dame, and the Bruins all saw their stock rise significantly following recent results. UCLA moved up four spots to No. 4 after a 34-20 victory over Minnesota. The Bruins are now one of only two unbeaten teams left in major college football, joining Utah at No. 2. Indiana suffered a steep fall, dropping five spots to No. 9 despite not playing last weekend. The committee chair said the shift was a correction based on new data from the weekend’s games. Why the Top Spot Changed Hands Georgia took over No. 1 ranking after blowing out Mississippi on Nov. 7. The Bulldogs had lost the top spot the week before, but their performance in Oxford, Miss., erased any doubt about their status. Hunter Yurachek, who leads the 13-person selection committee, said the move reflected the team’s strength rather than an admission of error from the previous week. Georgia’s defense and offense both looked strong enough to handle any opponent in the 12-team playoff format. Notre Dame also made a big jump, rising six spots to No. 5. The Irish leapfrogged Miami after beating the Hurricanes last weekend. Notre Dame’s win proved that the Irish could handle a top-tier opponent on the road. The committee rewarded the Irish for their resilience and their ability to close out a tough game against a rival. The Miami Drop and the UCLA Rise Miami’s fall to No. 7 was the most painful result for fans of the Canes. They lost by a single touchdown on the road and were missing their best player, Malachi Toney. The injury to Toney likely hurt their game planning and execution. Even with heavy losses, the team could not hold onto the top spot because other teams won their games decisively. “You have that combination of Miami losing as a No. 1 team and then five teams behind them having some signature wins,” Yurachek said, according to the New York Post . Moving those winning teams ahead of Miami was deemed the right decision by the committee. When a number one team loses, the field opens up for everyone else to make a claim. Five teams behind Miami all won their games, and the math forced a reshuffle. UCLA’s rise to No. 4 was even more dramatic. item.title: Signing Day: Ranking top classes, players for Class of 2027
item.description: Most years, the No. 1 recruit in NCAA men’s golf is up for discussion. This year, there is no debate. Miles Russell isn’t just the unquestioned top-ranked player in the Class of 2027 as the week-long early signing period starts Wednesday; the 18-year-old from Jacksonville Beach, Florida, might be the best college prospect in over a decade. He will sign with the Florida State Seminoles, who also have the No. 1 class, which includes top European recruit Edwin Askerfors, Tiger Woods’ son Charlie Woods and instate product Kaden Puranik. Close behind its rival is Florida, which inks Nos. 2 and 3 in the class, Jessy Huebner and Giuseppe Puebla. North Carolina also boasts two top-10 signees in No. 5 Dawson Lew and No. 9 Evan Liu. The surprise on the men’s side is Purdue, as head coach Andrew Sapp reels in No. 10 Sam Carraher as well as No. 38 Andy Dai and Gary Gu, who could easily make an argument for the top 50. Most shocking, though, was Asterisk Talley, the top-ranked girls junior, not signing with Stanford for now. Talley remains committed as she weighs her options, leaving the Cardinal to sign only No. 2 Anna Fang. That knocks Stanford down to the No. 4 class behind No. 1 UCLA, No. 2 Wake Forest and No. 3 Texas. The Bruins and Longhorns are the only programs to ink a pair of top-10 signings while the Demon Deacons will bring in No. 1 Amelia Zalsman as an early enrollee this spring. Madeleine Conser, ranked fourth in the class, will travel from her home in Portland, Oregon, to Kentucky for her college golf. She’s easily the Wildcats’ highest-rated recruit ever. Duke’s Ava Zhang reclassified from the Class of 2028 to sign with the Blue Devils for 2027. item.title: Manager praises new Arsenal loanee after debut
item.description: Manager praises new Arsenal loanee after debut Arsenal youngster Khari Ranson began a short-term loan move to Billericay Town on Tuesday night, and he’s already made his debut for the club. Photo via Ranson on Instagram Arsenal confirmed on Tuesday that 19-year-old goalkeeper Khari Ranson has joined National League South side Billericay Town on an initial 28-day loan. The teenager was straight into the action with his new side later that night, making the starting lineup for an Essex Senior Cup match against Little Oakley FC . The debut couldn’t have gone much better, with Ranson keeping a clean sheet as his new team won 7-0 to reach the quarter-finals. Photo via Ranson on Instagram Manager Danny Scopes was pleased, telling the media that “Khari in goal did well”. But there will be tougher tests to come than eighth-tier side Little Oakley over the course of the next four weeks. The schedule is helping to ease Ranson in, as Billericay’s next fixture is another cup game against lower-league opponents. On Saturday, Billericay will face another eighth-tier side in Waltham Abbey in the FA Trophy. After that, Billericay will return to their National League South campaign, the sixth tier of English football. Their next league game is against high-flying Truro City , and Ranson is likely to be tested a lot more in that game. Photo via Ranson on Instagram Ranson had made seven appearances for the Arsenal u21s this season, prior to his loan move. This loan spell is offering him his first taste of senior football, and it’s not impossible the two clubs could look to extend it when it ends next month. Photo via Ranson on Instagram

item.title: Tributes pour in for longtime Iona basketball announcer Gary Stanley
item.description: Credit: Iona Athletic Gary Stanley, the voice of the Iona Gaels men’s basketball team for over three decades, has passed away at 73. The Iona men’s basketball account shared the news on social media. “Iona Athletics mourns the passing of Gary Stanley, a longtime voice of Iona and Gaels men’s basketball,” read the post. “Gary’s passion for Iona and memorable presence behind the microphone made him an important part of the Gael family. His contributions will not be forgotten. Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with Gary’s family, friends, and all who had the privilege of knowing him.” Iona Athletics mourns the passing of Gary Stanley, a longtime voice of Iona and Gaels men’s basketball. Gary’s passion for Iona and memorable presence behind the microphone made him an important part of the Gael family. His contributions will not be forgotten. Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with Gary’s family, friends and all who had the privilege of knowing him. Rest in peace, Gary. — Iona Men’s Basketball (@IonaGaelsMBB) November 9, 2026 Starting in 1985, Stanley served for over three decades as the radio play-by-play announcer for Iona, calling games for WVOX and 93.5 WRTN, most notably alongside analyst Ed Ingles. After Ingles retired, Stanley continued calling Iona games alongside rotating analysts such as Bill Daughtry, Vin Parise, and Kevin Hamilton. Stanley was also a longtime sportscaster and anchor on WCBS 880 AM in New York. He worked directly for the all-news station for four years before moving to Shadow Traffic (later Clear Channel’s Total Traffic), and remained one of WCBS’s lead sports voices until 2013. His son, Casey Stanley , spent two stints as an assistant coach at Iona, including some time under Rick Pitino, and is currently the head coach of the Division II Westminster Griffins. He also shared a message about his father’s passing on social media. https://t.co/NHgNboWM9Y — Casey Stanley (@CoachStanleyWU) November 10, 2026 As news of his passing spread on social media, many of Stanley’s co-workers and peers in the sports media world offered tributes. @IonaGaelsMBB So sad to hear. Gary loved Iona and we met during a couple of NCAA @MarchMadnessMBB runs years ago. RIP Gary — Tim Brando (@TimBrando) November 10, 2026 I truly believe Gary could have done PxP anywhere. He was that good. It was a treat visiting with him and Ed Ingles before Manhattan/Iona games. Gary was tough – but earning his respect meant a great deal. I’ll miss him. — Ed Cohen (@edcohensports) November 10, 2026 Oh God, this is awful. Many a night was spent with Gary before an Iona game lamenting the Rangers’ struggles over the years. He and the late great Ed Ingles were two of the first friends I made covering the MAAC. My condolences to his son, @CoachStanleyWU, and his family. RIP. — Jaden Daly (@DalyDoseOfHoops) November 9, 2026 The post Tributes pour in for longtime Iona basketball announcer Gary Stanley, dead at 73 appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Why I recommend the Seestar S30 Plus smart telescope for beginners — full review
item.description: null I’ve used several smart telescopes over the last few years, but I'd recommend the ZWO Seestar S30 Plus to almost anyone wanting to get started in astrophotography. At $499/€499, it’s a complete imaging system that can photograph galaxies, nebulae and star clusters automatically, even from a light-polluted city. Better still, it’s so small that it can live on a bookshelf. The Pleiades (M45), photographed in mosaic mode with the Seestar S30 Plus. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) Jamie Carter The Andromeda Galaxy (M31) photographed using the Seestar S30 Plus. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) Jamie Carter The Dumbbell Nebula (M27) photographed using the Seestar S30 Plus. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) Jamie Carter I recently captured images of the Dumbbell Nebula (M27), the North America Nebula (NGC 7000), the Andromeda Galaxy (M31) and the Pleiades (M45) with the S30 Plus. All were remarkably easy to capture, and none of the images accompanying this review required external processing. It’s basically point-and-shoot astrophotography — if you live under light-polluted skies, that’s a game-changer. Star trails photographed using the Seestar S30 Plus’s dedicated Star Trail mode. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) (Image credit: Jamie Carter) I also think the S30 Plus makes an ideal companion to a conventional optical telescope. I can set it to photograph a nebula I have no hope of seeing under light pollution while I try to find brighter objects through the eyepiece of another telescope. It will then get on with collecting photons while I enjoy observing. For anyone who already owns a telescope but doesn’t want the expense and complexity of conventional astrophotography, that’s a compelling proposition. I photographed nebulas despite light pollution The S30 Plus is Seestar’s new entry-level smart telescope. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) (Image credit: Jamie Carter) One problem with buying a cheap optical telescope is that deep-sky objects rarely resemble the colorful photographs you see online. The moon, planets and bright star clusters can look wonderful through an eyepiece, but faint galaxies and nebulas are much harder to appreciate, particularly from a town or city. Like all smart telescopes, the S30 Plus gets around that problem by photographing objects rather than showing them directly. Its camera takes repeated exposures, which the telescope automatically stacks to reduce noise and gradually reveal faint detail. The longer you leave it working, the better the resulting image tends to become. Being able to photograph colorful nebulas without traveling to a remote observing site is one of the biggest attractions of the S30 Plus. For beginners living in cities, it could transform their experience of astronomy. It’s the perfect companion to my optical telescope The North America Nebula (NGC 7000) photographed using the Seestar S30 Plus. item.title: NASA's new UVEX space telescope will peer deep into the universe's most violent events
item.description: null A new NASA space telescope will study the universe in ultraviolet light to reveal the violent and turbulent events that bubble under what appears to be a cosmic sea of tranquility. The Ultraviolet Explorer (UVEX) mission, developed by NASA in conjunction with the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), will be the first mission to create deep all-sky maps in ultraviolet light. Thus, when it launches in 2031, UVEX will join new sky-mapping surveys like NASA's SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer), which scans the cosmos in infrared, and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, which does the same over the southern hemisphere in visible light, in creating deep-sky maps across a broad swathe of the electromagnetic spectrum. UVEX's ultraviolet views will reveal explosive events such as the collisions between ultra-dense stellar corpses called neutron stars and the supernova explosions that mark the deaths of massive stars and the births of neutron stars and black holes. Additionally, the NASA ultraviolet telescope should be able to detect a multitude of low-mass galaxies much closer to the Milky Way than similar galaxies that are currently being observed millions and even billions of light-years away by NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) . The $590 million UVEX mission will "advance fundamental frontiers in astrophysics, from understanding the smallest galaxies to diagnosing the aftermath of neutron-star mergers and other cosmic explosions," the mission's principal investigator, Caltech physics professor Fiona Harrison, said in an Oct. 27 statement . "The first major ultraviolet space mission in two decades, UVEX is a bold leap forward in our exploration of the ultraviolet universe," Caltech President Ray Jayawardhana said in the same statement. UVEX will paint a picture of cosmic life, death and afterlife UVEX will benefit from a major leap forward in UV sensitivity thanks to its Caltech-built sensors, which are based on complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) imaging technology. This will help the spacecraft tap into what Harrison described as "the untapped opportunity in the UV." UVEX will be uniquely poised to spot millions of nearby, small, and faint galaxies that are teeming with infant stars that emit bright UV light. "In optical light, it's very hard to distinguish these nearby galaxies from faraway ones that look similar," Harrison said. "UV light will make them easier to find." UVEX won't just be investigating the infancy of stars , however. It will also examine the deaths of ancient stars in the form of supernovas. The supernova relic Pa 30, as seen by the Gemini north telescope. (Image credit: International Gemini Observatory/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA) Supernovas occur when a massive star runs out of fuel for nuclear fusion and can no longer support itself against the inward push of its own gravity. As the core of the star collapses, its outer layers are blasted outward

item.title: Otti urges lawyers to defend rights of vulnerable Nigerians
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, has urged legal practitioners across the country to prioritise access to justice by extending legal services to indigent and vulnerable citizens who cannot afford legal representation. Otti made the call in Umuahia while declaring open the 2026 Nigerian Bar Association Section on Public Interest and Development Law (NBA-SPIDEL) Annual Conference, with the theme, “In Public Interest: Advancing Justice, Democracy and Development.” The governor urged lawyers to adopt a more humane approach to cases involving indigent and vulnerable citizens, stressing that the pursuit of justice should take precedence over professional interests and financial considerations. He said the legal profession had a responsibility to provide assistance to people who lacked the financial capacity to defend their rights. “And because you are lawyers, we need to go the extra mile of asking ourselves, beyond all the things that have been said, how can we be of service to people who cannot pay? “How can we be of service to the vulnerable? How can we help people who on their own cannot afford to help themselves? “Until government gets to that level, we have not cracked the surface. If it is only about you and then the money you make and all that, then you don’t need to be here. You may as well go and do something else,” he said. Otti said his administration had discovered cases of people who remained in correctional facilities despite allegedly having committed no offences warranting their continued detention. He cited the case of an individual who was allegedly detained for supporting an opposition political party, adding that the experience prompted him to direct the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice to work with the Chief Judge to secure the release of such inmates. The governor also warned against the misuse of the justice system to punish citizens for expressing their opinions or engaging in activities on social media, insisting that the protection of individual rights must remain central to governance. On judicial infrastructure, Otti disclosed that his administration would soon commission 10 newly constructed courthouses equipped with renewable energy systems, digitalised court records and broadband connectivity. He also urged lawyers to embrace technological advancements and prepare for emerging changes in legal practice. In his keynote address, former Vice President, Prof. Yemi Osinbajo, urged lawyers to move beyond litigation and legal interpretation to champion public interest, protect disadvantaged citizens and ensure that democracy delivers tangible benefits to the people. Osinbajo identified expensive legal services, prolonged court proceedings, judicial corruption and impunity as major obstacles to access to justice. He advocated people-centred reforms that would make legal services more affordable and accessible to ordinary Nigerians. Earlier, the President of the Nigerian Bar Associati
