item.title: 17 rescued, one injured as CNG commercial bus explodes on Lagos–Ibadan Expressway
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni At least ​17 people, including a driver, were rescued unhurt on Wednesday after a Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)-powered commercial bus burst into flames following a gas explosion at Berger Bus Stop along the Lagos-bound section of the Lagos–Ibadan Expressway. ​One male passenger, who was seated at the rear of the fully loaded Hiace bus (registration number EKY 798 YK), sustained severe burn injuries and was rushed to the Lagos State Trauma and Emergency Centre at Toll Gate for urgent medical attention. ​According to eyewitnesses, the vehicle was conveying 18 occupants from the Mowe-Ibafo axis toward Lagos when it erupted into flames, triggering panic among passengers and motorists. Commenting on the accident, Lagos State Traffic Management Authority, LASTMA General Manager, Olalekan Bakare-Oki, through Director of Public Affairs and Enlightenment, Adebayo Taofiq, LASTMA personnel promptly mobilised to the scene to evacuate the occupants, while officers of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service extinguished the blaze to prevent it from spreading. Personnel from the Ojodu Police Division also provided security and maintained order throughout the rescue and firefighting operations. ​Commending the operation, Bakare-Oki praised the agency’s personnel for their swift intervention and thanked the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service and the Nigeria Police Force for their collaboration. ​He noted that the incident underscores the importance of rapid emergency response and inter-agency synergy in mitigating road disasters. Bakare-Oki therefore urged commercial transport operators—particularly those running CNG-powered vehicles—to prioritise regular professional inspections, adhere to safety standards, and ensure the proper maintenance of their gas storage and delivery systems. The post 17 rescued, one injured as CNG commercial bus explodes on Lagos–Ibadan Expressway appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Gov Yusuf presents N1.107trn 2027 budget, earmarks 63% for capital projects
item.description: Sekinat Osundiji Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, has presented a proposed budget of N1.107 trillion for the 2027 fiscal year to the state House of Assembly. The budget, tagged “Budget of Consolidating Gains and Accelerated Rural Development,” is the fourth and final budget of the administration’s first tenure, which is expected to end on May 29, 2027. Presenting the estimates, Yusuf said the budget was designed to consolidate existing achievements, accelerate rural development and ensure the completion of ongoing projects before the expiration of his administration’s first term. The governor said his administration had achieved more than 90 per cent of the programmes, projects and policies outlined in its development blueprint. He, however, acknowledged that some commitments remained outstanding, adding that the 2027 budget would prioritise their completion, alongside strengthening essential public services. “This is not merely nominal. It is a fiscal commitment to ensure that no ongoing project is abandoned,” he said. He added that the budget would consolidate reforms in free education, primary healthcare revitalisation and urban renewal, while ensuring that residents benefit from government projects and programmes. Yusuf said the proposed budget would focus on education, healthcare, infrastructure, agriculture, water supply and human capital development, which he described as central to improving productivity and living conditions in the state. Budget breakdown Giving a breakdown of the proposed expenditure, the governor said ₦693.47 billion was earmarked for capital expenditure, while ₦413.55 billion was allocated to recurrent expenditure. He said the proposed capital-to-recurrent expenditure ratio was 63 per cent to 37 per cent, reflecting the administration’s intention to direct more resources towards infrastructure and other development projects while meeting its recurrent obligations. On revenue projections, Yusuf put the state’s total recurrent revenue at ₦692.64 billion, comprising ₦142.84 billion from internally generated revenue and revenue from the Federation Account. He said the projected recurrent revenue represented a 34 per cent decrease compared with the 2026 fiscal year. However, he projected a 73 per cent increase in internally generated revenue, attributing the growth to reforms at the Kano State Internal Revenue Service, including digital revenue administration and the expansion of the Easy Tax digitisation initiative. The governor further said the state expected ₦354.38 billion in capital receipts from grants and loans, alongside an opening balance of ₦60 billion to finance the proposed budget. He said the allocations would support projects and programmes across the state’s economic and social sectors. Yusuf added that the government would prioritise completing ongoing projects and strengthening existing programmes before the end of its first tenure in May 2027. item.title: Man Utd ‘reach verbal agreement’ with Pochettino to replace Carrick
item.description: Manchester United have reportedly reached a “verbal agreement in principle” with Mauricio Pochettino to replace Michael Carrick as their manager in a bid to revive the fortunes of the struggling English giants. Carrick’s position at Old Trafford has been the subject of intense speculation following United’s worst start to a season in 40 years, leaving them languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after an eight-match winless run. He remains in post but it is believed Carrick’s future will be decided at a meeting attended by influential shareholder Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox in Monaco on Wednesday. Berrada and Wilcox are reportedly leaning towards dismissing Carrick. United States head coach Pochettino has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. It was only three months ago, however, that Pochettino signed a contract extension to remain with the United States through to the 2030 World Cup. US Soccer would be due compensation should he move to Manchester, with the 54-year-old understood to have a $10 million (£7.5 million) release clause. But Sky Sports reported Wednesday that United have “reached a verbal agreement in principle” with Pochettino, linked with a move to Old Trafford on several previous occasions, to become their new head coach. – Turbulent reign – Carrick was seen arriving at United’s Carrington training ground on Wednesday but it appears to be only a matter of time before his turbulent reign comes to an end. The 45-year-old had been granted a stay of execution after he was widely expected to be axed in late October following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth. But United were beaten 2-0 at Chelsea, then scrambled a last-gasp 3-2 win against Roma in the Champions League after falling two goals down. It appeared former United and England midfielder Carrick would be on the way out when his team twice trailed Aston Villa by two goals on Sunday. When United scored twice in stoppage-time to rescue an improbable 4-4 draw, it was interpreted as a positive sign for Carrick as the players were still fighting for him. But a change now appears likely, with former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe, ex-Chelsea chief Antonio Conte and former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann also linked with the United job. United have the rest of the two-week international break to resolve their managerial situation before returning to action at bitter rivals Liverpool on November 22. Carrick has presided over United’s slide to 18th place — their lowest position 10 games into a top-flight season since 1986/87 when they were 20th. He was hired on a permanent basis in the close-season after leading United to a third-place finish in the Premier League during his spell as interim boss. item.title: Prison Break actor Stacy Keach dies at 85
item.description: American actor Stacy Keach, renowned for his roles in television and film productions spanning more than six decades, has died at the age of 85. Keach died on Tuesday at his home in Magdalenka, Poland, following a prolonged battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure. His wife, Małgosia Tomassi Keach, announced his death in a statement, describing him as a courageous fighter whose resilience defined both his personal life and acting career. “It is with profound sadness and a broken heart that I announce the passing of my darling husband, Stacy Keach. After a long and difficult battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure, Stacy peacefully departed this world,” she said. She described the late actor as a legendary performer whose work earned him admiration from audiences worldwide, adding that his death had left an immeasurable void in the family. Keach began his acting career on Broadway in the 1960s before transitioning to film in the 1970s. He gained recognition for his performance alongside Faye Dunaway in the 1971 film Doc. He became particularly popular for portraying private investigator Mike Hammer in several television productions, including Mickey Spillane’s Mike Hammer and The New Mike Hammer. His other notable screen appearances included the television series Prison Break, Blue Bloods and Titus, as well as films such as The Long Riders, Nebraska and The Bourne Legacy. The actor also appeared in the biblical miniseries Jesus of Nazareth, where he portrayed Barabbas. Over a career spanning approximately 60 years, Keach accumulated more than 200 film and television credits and earned recognition as an accomplished interpreter of Shakespeare. His career also included stage performances and a Tony Award nomination, further establishing his reputation as a versatile actor. Keach came from a family with strong ties to the entertainment industry. His father, Stacy Keach Sr., was a respected actor, while his brother, James Keach, is also an actor and filmmaker. He was previously reported to have suffered a heart attack on stage in Chicago in 2017. Keach is survived by his wife, Małgosia, their children, Karolina and Shannon, grandchildren and other members of the extended family. In her tribute, his wife said his unforgettable voice, remarkable spirit and love for his family would remain with them forever. The post Prison Break actor Stacy Keach dies at 85 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Meagan Good & Jonathan Majors Look Picture-Perfect at AFRIFF in Lagos
item.description: Meagan Good and Jonathan Majors coordinating in neutral tones and a red cap accent for AFRIFF. Who knew an ivory mini dress and a classic black suit could make such an interesting pairing? During their time in Lagos for AFRIFF, Meagan Good and Jonathan Majors posed for a studio portrait in two looks that took very different approaches to dressing up. Meagan’s dress brought together colourful beadwork, a fitted silhouette and a floor-length train, while Jonathan opted for black tailoring, an open-neck white shirt and a red cap. And while his outfit keeps things relatively simple, there’s nothing ordinary about the details of hers. Let’s start with Meagan’s dress, because there is quite a lot happening here. At first glance, the ivory mini might seem relatively simple, but look a little closer and the details begin to unfold. The fitted halter-neck bodice is covered in rows of turquoise, bronze and dark green beads, arranged horizontally to follow the shape of her waist. Then there’s the skirt, which takes a more unexpected turn with clusters of dark beaded embellishments scattered across the fabric. And just when you think you’ve taken it all in, an extended panel falls from the side of the mini skirt, creating a long, floor-sweeping train. It’s a fun combination of short and dramatic, with the beadwork giving the dress plenty to say without needing much else. Meagan Good styled in a sculpted halter-neck corset dress featuring multi-coloured beaded detailing and a side train. Meagan kept the rest of her styling fairly simple. Black ankle-strap heels and a textured black clutch were her accessories of choice, while her voluminous curls were left loose around her shoulders. Her bronze-toned makeup and glossy nude lip tied everything together without competing with the dress. Jonathan went in a completely different direction, keeping things classic with a black jacket and matching trousers over a white shirt, worn open at the neck. A grey patterned scarf added another detail around the collar, while his light-framed sunglasses and black patent shoes completed the outfit. But it’s the red cap that really changes the look. Against all that black and white, it gives the outfit a welcome hit of colour and makes the styling feel more personal. Meagan Good and Jonathan Majors showcasing intricate beaded dress embroidery and red cap styling. It’s an interesting pairing: Meagan’s dress has all the beadwork, colour and movement, while Jonathan’s outfit is built around simple tailoring and a few well-chosen accessories. There’s plenty to appreciate in both, wouldn’t you agree? Meagan Good displaying horizontal beadwork in turquoise and bronze paired with bronze-toned makeup. *** Photo Credit: Amplify Africa/Instagram The post Meagan Good & Jonathan Majors Look Picture-Perfect at AFRIFF in Lagos appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. item.title: Liverpool should have had penalty for shirt-pull on Isak – Panel
item.description: Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty for the shirt-pull on Alexander Isak in their Premier League match against Arsenal, an expert panel ruled Wednesday. The Sweden striker’s shirt was tugged by Gunners defender Jurrien Timber in the match at Anfield on November 1, which Premier League champions Arsenal won 1-0. Referee Andy Madley let the incident pass without sanction, and video assistant referee Stuart Attwell decided against recommending a review. The decision was criticised at the time by pundits such as Jamie Carragher and Ian Wright, and now the five-person Key Match Incidents panel has said a penalty should have been awarded. Madley’s decision was criticised by four of the panellists, who felt Timber’s challenge met the threshold for a holding offence, while three felt Attwell should have intervened because it was a clear and obvious error by Madley. Isak did not make any protest about Timber’s shirt-pull to the on-field officials, in a match which was settled by Kai Havertz’s goal for the Gunners. Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola, asked after the match whether Isak should have gone down following the challenge, replied: “It’s a shame you ask me this question, but honestly, yes, we have to tell them (the players), go down, because they (the officials) are not going to call it otherwise. “And then referees complain why they go down. Because if you don’t go down, you don’t call it. Then it’s like, no, you are all the time going down. “But I think Alex is honest. He tries to go for the ball, everyone can see live straight away there is a clear, clear pull.” The post Liverpool should have had penalty for shirt-pull on Isak – Panel appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Throwback: 10 songs that have defined Nigeria’s Detty December
item.description: Before the December concert rush, packed nightclubs, beach parties and returning diaspora crowds became synonymous with Detty December, Nigerian music had already established the festive season as its biggest playground. Every December, a new collection of songs takes over the streets, clubs, weddings, concerts and parties, providing the soundtrack to the celebrations as Nigerians round off the year. From Wizkid’s infectious melodies and Naira Marley’s street anthems to Portable’s Zazoo Zeh and Seyi Vibez’s Chance, some records have become inseparable from memories of particular festive seasons. READ MORE: Although Nigerians have celebrated Christmas and New Year with music and parties for decades, the phrase Detty December gained popularity around 2016, with singer Mr Eazi credited with popularising it through his concert promotion. Over the years, the culture has grown into a major entertainment season, with Lagos becoming a destination for returning Nigerians, international visitors and music lovers. As another festive season approaches, here is a throwback to 10 songs that have defined Nigeria’s Detty December experience over the years. 1. 2016 – Mad Over You by Runtown Few songs captured the mood of the 2016 festive season quite like Runtown’s ‘Mad Over You’. Released towards the end of the year, the song became a massive hit, with its Ghana-inspired Pon Pon sound, catchy melody and romantic lyrics making it a favourite across clubs, parties and radio stations. The record arrived at a time when Nigerian music was embracing a more melodic, highlife-influenced sound, moving away from some of the faster dance-driven records that had dominated previous years. Its popularity extended beyond Nigeria, becoming a major hit across West Africa and one of the songs many music lovers associate with the early Detty December era. 2. 2017 – Manya by Mut4y featuring Wizkid Wizkid returned to the festive-season conversation in 2017 with ‘Manya’, a collaboration with producer Mut4y. Built around an infectious rhythm and an interpolation of the popular Ghanaian song ‘Akohoma Womu’, the track quickly became a party favourite. Released during a year in which Wizkid enjoyed significant international recognition with his ‘Sounds From the Other Side’ project, ‘Manya’ helped maintain his dominance on the Nigerian music scene. From clubs to concerts and street parties, the song became one of the defining sounds of the 2017 festive season, competing with Kizz Daniel’s ‘Yeba’ and Reekado Banks’ ‘Like’. 3. 2018 – Able God by Chinko Ekun featuring Lil Kesh and Zlatan If there was one street anthem that Nigerians could hardly escape during the 2018 festive season, it was ‘Able God’. Chinko Ekun recruited Lil Kesh and Zlatan for the Rexxie-produced record, which became popular for its energetic delivery, memorable hook and danceable production. The song arrived during the rise of street-pop and the Zanku dance movement, helping introduce Zlatan to a much wider audience. It

item.title: Nearly 64,000 Nigerians flee to Niger over insecurity – UNHCR
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Nearly 64,000 Nigerians have fled their homes and crossed into neighbouring Niger Republic since the beginning of 2026 to escape escalating violence involving Islamist militants and armed criminal gangs, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) has disclosed. The UN refugee agency, in a briefing issued on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, warned that the growing influx was creating a deepening humanitarian and protection crisis in Niger, which is already hosting more than 500,000 refugees and asylum-seekers. According to UNHCR, approximately 327,500 Nigerians are already seeking refuge in Niger, while several hundred others have reportedly crossed into neighbouring Benin Republic because of worsening insecurity in northern Nigeria. The agency’s Director of External Relations, Dominique Hyde, said most of the newly arrived Nigerians had settled in the border regions of Diffa, in southeastern Niger, and Tahoua, in the western part of the country. In October alone, about 1,200 Nigerians crossed into Diffa, while another 3,400 arrived in Tahoua. UNHCR disclosed that more than 23,000 people, over two-thirds of them children, had arrived in Diffa since the beginning of the year. The agency expressed concern over the difficult conditions facing the displaced families, many of whom are living in makeshift shelters without adequate food, clean drinking water, healthcare and other essential services. It said some women were forced to walk several kilometres daily to fetch water for their families, while humanitarian organisations had reported increasing cases of malnutrition, respiratory infections and poor sanitation among the new arrivals. The refugee agency also raised concerns over the registration of displaced Nigerians, revealing that only about five per cent of those who arrived in Niger this year had been formally registered. The absence of proper documentation, it warned, was making it difficult for thousands of refugees to access humanitarian assistance and essential public services. The situation is further complicated by insecurity and climate-related challenges in Niger, particularly in the Diffa region, where more than 70 per cent of the country’s reported security incidents this year have occurred. Despite the growing humanitarian pressure, UNHCR acknowledged the support provided by Niger’s authorities and host communities, including the allocation of land for temporary shelters. The agency, however, appealed for increased international assistance, seeking $11.4 million to expand its humanitarian response in Niger, Nigeria and Benin. The appeal includes $2 million for immediate critical interventions covering food, water, shelter, healthcare, refugee registration and protection. UNHCR warned that without additional funding, thousands of vulnerable families fleeing violence could be left without essential humanitarian assistance. item.title: Xenophobic attacks: Help South Africans, don’t punish them — OAU don
item.description: …As varsity’s International Relations Department marks 50th anniversary By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Federal Government has been urged to adopt a sympathetic approach towards South Africa over the recent xenophobic attacks, rather than resort to punitive measures, with a don at the Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), Ile-Ife, saying South Africans need help at a difficult time. A Professor of International Relations at OAU, Charles Ukeje, said the xenophobic violence was regrettable, particularly given Nigeria’s significant contributions, alongside other African countries, to the struggle against apartheid in South Africa. Ukeje spoke during a press conference organised to herald the 50th anniversary of the university’s Department of International Relations at the campus. He blamed the attacks partly on the failure of successive South African governments to adequately educate their citizens about the sacrifices made by Nigeria and other African countries towards ending apartheid. According to him, proper education about the contributions of other African nations could have helped foster a stronger sense of brotherhood among South Africans and other Africans. He said: “I believe that the xenophobic violence in South Africa is very regrettable. It is regrettable because this is a country which the rest of the continent, particularly Nigeria, helped to midwife in the context of apartheid. “So, in the post-apartheid era, you would expect that the South Africans will be more and better disposed to the rest of Africans, given the amount of sacrifice that Nigerians and other African countries have made in the bid to end apartheid in that country. “It is regrettable that generations of South African leaders, upon achieving an end to apartheid, really did not adequately educate their citizens on the role the whole of Africa played. “Perhaps, if they had done that, things would have been different. Perhaps, the ordinary South African citizens on the street would treat and see other Africans as brothers.” On Nigeria’s response, the don said the country should maintain its longstanding commitment to Africa as the centrepiece of its foreign policy. He urged the Federal Government to demonstrate leadership by showing understanding towards South Africa, despite the hostility some of its citizens might harbour towards Nigerians. “In terms of how Nigeria should respond, Africa has always been the centrepiece of Nigeria’s foreign policy. I don’t think that is going to change. “I think Nigeria has the responsibility to continue to see itself as a leader on the continent. I think that role for Nigeria is perhaps more important today than it was anytime. “And I’m looking forward to the Nigerian government not really wielding the big stick against South Africa, but to actually acknowledge that the country and its citizens are facing very difficult circumstances at this time and we need to be more sympathetic to them, even with the amount of disdain that the ordinary ci

item.title: Lagos govt warns PSPs over refuse crisis, demands results
item.description: …..As Solus, Olusosun dumpsites resume operations …PSPs to deploy over 700 trucks By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has warned Private Sector Participation (PSP) waste operators to deliver immediate results or face enforcement measures, following the reopening of the Solus and Olusosun dumpsites after months of closure. The government said it had fulfilled its responsibility by rehabilitating the facilities and their access roads, leaving waste operators with no further excuses for the persistent refuse crisis across the state. Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, gave the warning on Wednesday during an inspection of the previously closed Solus dumpsite in Alimosho Local Government Area. Wahab said the government expected PSP operators to improve waste collection and evacuation across their areas of operation, stressing that residents deserved value for the services they paid for. “Too much is given, so much more is expected. There are no more excuses,” the commissioner said, recounting his message to the leadership of the PSP operators. “The state government has done its own bit; let your PSP members also put their skin in it and see how they can achieve what we set out jointly to achieve because they suggested we put this into play and now we’ve done it for them.” According to him, the decision to reopen Solus followed proposals by waste operators to rehabilitate the facility rather than wait for the development of new dumpsites around Badagry and Epe. He explained that Solus, located within Lagos West, serves several local government areas, including Alimosho, Ajeromi-Ifelodun, Mushin, Badagry, Ikeja, Ojo and Apapa. The commissioner said the contractor handling the rehabilitation had assured the government that the repaired access road would last at least one year, subject to quarterly maintenance. He added that the facility was expected to accommodate at least 100 trucks daily, significantly improving waste evacuation in the affected areas. “100 trucks from this axis coming here to discharge gives us the comfort that our streets, our homes will not be littered with waste,” Wahab said. Addressing complaints by residents over the failure of some PSP operators to collect refuse regularly, the commissioner said the state government would enforce its polluter-pays policy to ensure operators delivered the services for which residents paid. He warned that the government would take necessary measures to hold defaulting operators accountable. LAWMA restructuring Wahab also confirmed a major restructuring of the Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA), ordered by the state governor, as part of efforts to improve waste management operations. He announced the appointment of Juwon Akinyemi as Acting Managing Director, Dr Tjani Olorunwa as Acting Executive Director of Operations, and Kunle Adebiyi as substantive Executive Director of Finance. item.title: ADC protesters take Mark judgment dispute to NJC, UN, EU, UK, US embassies
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Members of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) on Wednesday staged a protest at the Federal High Court in Abuja, demanding the release of the Certified True Copy (CTC) of the judgment nullifying the party’s National Working Committee led by former Senate President, David Mark. The protesters accused the trial judge, Justice Peter Lifu, of withholding the November 5 judgment despite an application by the party’s lawyers and payment of the prescribed fees, arguing that the delay was frustrating their efforts to challenge the ruling at the Court of Appeal. The protesters also extended their campaign beyond the court premises, storming the headquarters of the United Nations (UN), as well as the European Union (EU), United Kingdom and United States embassies in Abuja, where they submitted letters seeking diplomatic attention and support for what they described as due process, the right of appeal and credible elections in Nigeria. The letters bore the subject: “Urgent Appeal for Diplomatic Attention and Support for Due Process, the Right of Appeal and Credible Elections in Nigeria – Re: Judgment Delivered on 5th November, 2026 in Suit No: FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025 (Nafiu Bala Gombe Vs. ADC & Ors).” Speaking during the protest, a former Acting Chairman of the ADC in the Federal Capital Territory, Yusuf Shehu Tijani, described the judgment as a sham and called on the National Judicial Council (NJC) to intervene. “Our reason for coming here today is what Justice Lifu is doing. He is holding on to the sham judgment he said he passed. He should send the CTC, so that we can get it and appeal the judgment. “Moreover, the Supreme Court already affirmed the leadership of Senator David Mark as the National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress. So why is the High Court going against that recognition, saying he’s passing a judgment? “Now the judgment you passed, give us the Certified True Copy so that we can appeal. He is refusing to do that. That is why we are here,” Tijani said. He said the protest was intended to draw the NJC’s attention to the alleged delay and compel the judge to release the document. “So the protest is to call on the NJC to pressure this man, let him do what is right, because justice must prevail in Nigeria. This is not a jungle. This is a country that has laws, that has rules, and we have to follow the Constitution of the country. “The stated law is that he should send the CTC so that we can appeal the judgment, which is a sham judgment in the first place,” he added. The protest followed a November 10 petition addressed to the Chief Judge of the Federal High Court, Justice John Tsoho, by members of the ADC candidates’ forum, demanding the immediate release of the judgment. In the petition signed by Audu Aliyu on behalf of the candidates, the group said its lawyers applied for the CTC immediately after Justice Lifu delivered the judgment on November 5 and paid the prescribed fees, but had yet to receive the

item.title: Police probe Blord over armed officers’ escort
item.description: The Nigeria Police Force has launched an investigation into a viral video showing armed police officers escorting businessman Linus Williams, popularly known as Blord, at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport, Enugu. The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, described the deployment of the officers as “unlawful and illegal”, saying an investigation had commenced into the incident. Iniedu disclosed this in a statement posted on his official X account on Wednesday while reacting to the video. “Unlawful and illegal. Investigation has commenced into this incident please. We say #notoimpunity,” he wrote. The video, which Blord shared on his Instagram page on Tuesday, showed him arriving at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport in Enugu, accompanied by armed police officers dressed in camouflage uniforms and tactical gear. The businessman was seen wearing a red-and-white striped traditional cap associated with the Kwankwaso political brand. He was also seen arriving in a black Cadillac with the personalised number plate, “B-LORD”. Other scenes in the footage showed Blord walking alongside the armed officers at the airport and at other locations, including what appeared to be his business premises. The officers were seen providing him with an escort and opening the vehicle door for him. Captioning the video, Blord wrote: “Back to base, business as usual. From the airport to a brief stop at BlordGroup Enugu branch, then back to Awka. Every move has its purpose, and the vision never takes a break. Blord is home!” In another Instagram post, the businessman said he had been in Sabon Gari, Kano State, where he met his “brothers” before returning to Enugu. The development comes months after President Bola Tinubu ordered the withdrawal of police officers attached to Very Important Persons (VIPs) across the country and their redeployment to core policing duties. Tinubu gave the directive at a security meeting with service chiefs and the Director-General of the Department of State Services in Abuja on November 23, 2025. According to a statement by the President’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, VIPs requiring protection would henceforth be assigned armed operatives of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps instead of police officers. The President said the measure was aimed at strengthening police presence in communities, particularly those facing security challenges. On December 6, 2025, the police also deployed a Special Enforcement Team to monitor compliance with the directive, beginning with an operation in Lagos. The then Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Benjamin Hundeyin, said the exercise recorded no cases of unauthorised deployment of police escorts. item.title: Google gooses Python AI performance by... removing Python
item.description: "Train in Python, serve in C++" might as well be Google's motto when it comes to much of its ML work. Python is easy for data scientists to wield, but keeping its interpreter in the serving pipeline can add overhead and deployment headaches. The industry-backed OpenXLA Project provides tools for compiling machine learning computations into native code for different processors. The latest component of this setup to be open sourced is XSE , short for the XLA Serving Engine. One-shot inference XSE is not so much suited for large-scale LLM inference (which would be better served by vLLM or SGLang ), but rather for smaller, more sharply task-oriented models, of which there are plenty at Google. "LLM serving gets most of the attention right now, but a significant amount of production inference is still ranking, recommendation, embedding, and vision models. These tend to be short requests with very high [queries-per-second] and tight latency budgets," Nathan Beach , Google director of product management, wrote in a LinkedIn missive Tuesday. At Google, XSE already handles more than six million queries per second across services including YouTube Shorts, Google Ads, and Search. These models aren't there for a leisurely chat. They rank results, recommend videos, and make other decisions on the fly, often without users noticing. A Python interpreter mulling each request would be a bottleneck, if not the end of Google itself. In Google's tests on short requests, XSE delivered two to five times the throughput of its best optimized Python server, using a quarter of the memory. No Python here In this setup, the ML boffins write their model code in Python, using Google's JAX to help with the sums. Google also plans integration with TorchTPU so PyTorch users can export models for C++ serving on TPUs. An export tool packages the model's computations in StableHLO, a portable intermediate representation, alongside its trained weights in an "XLA SavedModel." Ready to precognate, the C++ serving runtime uses XLA to compile those computations into native code for the target silicon. No Python interpreter to see here. XLA SavedModels can run on GPUs and CPUs – Google partnered with both Arm and Intel to develop the XLA ecosystem. But Google obviously thinks it'd be a lot cooler if you ran your models on its own line of TPU accelerators . Python's sluggishness continues to be an issue for the ML community. Beyond XSE, other approaches have been taken, many of which involve jettisoning the Python code as quickly as possible. PyTorch offers a native C++ runtime called LibTorch . Also, Microsoft and its collaborators offer the ONNX Runtime , which supports an open graph format with Python bindings. Even Python's own reference implementation relies heavily on C, with Rust now getting a foot in the door. ®

item.title: Govt Scared of Peter Obi’s Popularity, Campaign Camp Pushes Back Over Flamingos Airport Encounter
item.description: Representatives of Peter Obi have dismissed accusations that the presidential candidate was “playing to the gallery” during a recent encounter with Nigeria’s national U-17 women’s football team, the Flamingos, at the airport. Addressing criticism from political opponents and government commentators, a representative for Obi’s camp said the incident was a spontaneous moment during routine domestic travel, claiming federal officials and the ruling party are unsettled by the opposition leader’s widespread public support. ‘A Man on the Move’ Rebutting claims that the airport greeting was a staged publicity stunt, Obi’s campaign team clarified that the candidate was at the airport to board a commercial flight for scheduled engagements across the country when he crossed paths with the victorious sports delegation. “I don’t understand what they mean by our candidate playing to the gallery,” the spokesperson said. “Every Nigerian knows that Peter Obi is a man on the move. He has engagements across the country, and at that time, he was at the airport just like any other traveller trying to catch a flight to his next destination.” The statement emphasised that meeting the Flamingos—who were returning from international competition—was entirely coincidental, adding that Obi’s decision to approach the team was an act of national pride. “It just so happened that the Flamingos were there at the same time, and like any patriotic Nigerian, he simply wanted to greet them and congratulate them on their victory.” Pattern of Restrictions The campaign further alleged that this was not an isolated event, asserting that security or administrative barriers have previously been used to prevent Obi from interacting with victorious Nigerian athletes during public appearances. Obi’s camp described the government’s reaction as indicative of political anxiety over his public visibility. “This is not the first time this has happened,” the representative noted. “He has been prevented from greeting victorious Nigerian athletes before. This latest incident just shows how jittery the government is. They do not want him taking the spotlight because wherever Peter Obi goes, Nigerians rally behind him.” ﻿ ﻿ Political Friction Ahead of Elections The clash underscores the heightened sensitivity surrounding public engagements and political optics as major parties structure their national campaigns. While government supporters have accused opposition figures of leveraging national sports achievements for political leverage, Obi’s campaign maintained that public enthusiasm during his travel movements remains organic and unscripted. “While it is understandable that they are scared, it is pathetic, to say the least,” the spokesperson concluded, reiterating that the presidential candidate will continue his scheduled nationwide tours and citizen engagements despite ongoing political scrutiny. item.title: 'France has some of the cleanest electricity in the world, but we're not using enough of it'
item.description: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Thierry Bros, energy & climate expert and Professor of Science and Economics at Sciences Po. As geopolitical conflicts unsettle global energy markets and governments struggle to reconcile climate commitments with economic and security imperatives, the answer lies in a fundamental reconsideration of the sequence of climate policy. "Electrification first," he argues, acknowledging that this "doesn't necessarily mean clean electricity." His argument is grounded in a critical assessment of international climate diplomacy and European energy policy. "We've seen many COPs, and they've all failed," he contends, questioning the effectiveness of ambitious targets that have yet to deliver the necessary structural transformation. In his view, electrification offers a more pragmatic route than some of the technological priorities previously championed by European policymakers.

item.title: What Are The Effective Ways of Using AI?
item.description: Two people engaging with technology in a contemporary hotel lobby work setting. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is changing how people learn, work, communicate and solve problems. In today’s world, if you’re not on board with AI, it could be said you’re being resistant to the fastest-growing technological innovation in the world. From students researching academic subjects to professionals developing business ideas, AI tools have become companions in everyday activities for people. They can help save time, explore new ideas, understand difficult concepts and approach tasks differently. However, as more people embrace these AI tools, it is important to understand that using AI effectively goes beyond knowing what prompts to enter. It requires knowing when to use it, how to question its responses and, most importantly, when to rely on your own knowledge and judgement. AI could make us better at what we do, not make us dependent on it. Here are ways we think you use AI effectively: Use AI as a Research Assistant One of the most effective ways to use AI is for research and information gathering. Whether you are writing an article, preparing a presentation or exploring an unfamiliar subject, AI can help you identify relevant topics, explain complex ideas and suggest areas worth investigating. You can ask it to break down unfamiliar concepts, identify key questions, or suggest research directions. However, do not treat every response as fact. Verify important information using credible sources, published research, books and reliable websites. AI can help you find information, but you are responsible for establishing what is true. Use AI to Brainstorm and Explore Ideas Like knowledge gathering, AI can brainstorm ideas with you. Sometimes, the hardest part of starting a project is knowing where to begin. AI can help you overcome this challenge by suggesting ideas, exploring different approaches and presenting perspectives you may not have considered. For writers, entrepreneurs, researchers and creatives, it can be a useful brainstorming partner. You can share an idea, ask questions about its strengths and weaknesses, and explore ways to develop it. However, brainstorming should not become an excuse to surrender your imagination. Let AI expand your thinking, not replace it. Use AI to Improve Your Work, Not Replace Your Skills This is becoming more important. AI can help you identify grammatical errors, improve sentence construction, organise information, summarise lengthy documents and make your communication clearer. It can reduce the time spent on repetitive tasks and create more room for important responsibilities. The important thing is that you should remain actively involved. Read what AI produces, question its suggestions and make the final decisions yourself. Your skills improve when you practise them, not when you consistently hand them over to a machine. For students, AI can explain difficult topics and provide feedback on your work. Protect Your C

item.title: From Lagos to Cotonou! BN’s Osas is Taking You Inside SIMA 2026
item.description: One thing you can always bet on, as far as BellaNaija is concerned, is our alignment with African culture, creativity, and the people shaping the continent’s stories. “For where our treasure is, our heart will be”. And this time around, our heart is in Cotonou! Oh, and so are we! Hey BNers! Osas Okonyon here, and I’m heading to the Republic of Benin for the third edition of the Salon des Industries Musicales d’Afrique Francophone (SIMA), where I’ll be over the next few days. SIMA is bringing together artists, music executives, producers, creatives, investors and other key players in the African music industry for conversations about the future of our sound, the business behind it, and how African music can continue to make its mark on the world. This year’s theme, “African Music: From the Stage to Global Influence,” is particularly exciting. Beyond the music we love and the artists we celebrate, there’s so much to explore about the business, opportunities, collaborations and structures that help African creativity thrive. From conversations around music financing, artificial intelligence and intellectual property to the intersections of music, fashion, film, tourism and sports, SIMA promises a fascinating look into the evolving creative landscape. So, whether you’re a music lover, a creative, an industry enthusiast or simply someone who loves experiencing Africa through its people and culture, come along with me. I’ll be bringing you the conversations, the discoveries, the behind-the-scenes moments and, of course, all the good vibes from Cotonou. Put on your seatbelts, BNers. We’re about to get into the sound and influence of African music! item.description:
Tariq is the Editor-in-Chief of Space.com based out of our New York City office and joined the team in 2001, first as an intern and staff writer, and later as an editor. He covers human spaceflight, exploration and space science, as well as skywatching and entertainment. He became Space.com's Managing Editor in 2009 and Editor-in-Chief in 2019. In October 2022, Tariq received the Harry Kolcum Award for excellence in space reporting from the National Space Club Florida Committee. In June 2025, the National Space Society awarded him the Space Pioneer Award for Excellence in Mass Media at the International Space Development Conference in Orlando, Florida.

Hailing from Stockton, California (where he attended the same high school as NASA astronaut Jose Hernandez), Tariq studied print journalism and astronomy at the University of Southern California in Los Angeles, earning a bachelor's degree in journalism in 1999 along with a minor in astronomy. He then served as a staff reporter for The Los Angeles Times covering education and city beats in La Habra and Fullerton in Orange County for the Our Times sections.

In 2000, Tariq became the city reporter for the Huntington Beach Independent, a weekly publication of the Los Angeles Times, covering local politics and events, crime, business and environmental issues. He left the Los Angeles Times in 2001 to study science journalism at New York University, where he earned a master's degree in 2002 from NYU's Science and Environmental Reporting Program (now the Science, Health and Environmental Reporting Program) under the direction of space reporter William Burrows.

Tariq first joined Space.com as an intern in September 2001 while also serving as a research assistant for nutrition writer Gary Taubes and writing freelance projects, where his work appeared in The Scientist and Laboratory Equipment Magazine. He became a full-time reporter covering spaceflight in 2004, with this first launch being NASA's STS-114 Return to Flight mission in July 2005.

Tariq is also an Eagle Scout (yes, he has the Space Exploration merit badge) and went to Space Camp four times as a kid and a fifth time as an adult. When not writing about space, you can find Tariq watching the latest Star Trek TV series, sci-fi movies and reading about hippos, his favorite animal. You can find Tariq at Space.com and as the co-host to the This Week In Space podcast with space historian Rod Pyle on the TWiT network. To see his latest project, you can follow Tariq on Twitter @tariqjmalik.

item.title: Linux joins Heathrow's grounded fleet of information screens
item.description: UK travelers had more than fog to contend with this week, as Linux proved that if Windows could bork anything, it could bork it better. Spotted by Andy Hinks at Heathrow Airport's Terminal 2, this information display has seen better days. While its neighbors offer walking times and terminal maps, it presents a sideways Linux boot log – useful only if your next connection involves mounting a filesystem. There aren't many clues to what has befallen the machine behind the screen. The boot messages mention systemd , an Intel PRO/1000 network adapter, and an EXT4 filesystem on what appears to be a logical volume named LV_ROOT . Whether mounting that filesystem is the problem, or simply the last thing displayed before something else went wrong, isn't clear. Heathrow's information displays clearly accommodate a mixture of technologies. Recent examples ran Microsoft Windows, which had - naturally - suffered a moment of its own. Linux can evidently be just as unreliable in the right hands. The question is which Linux distribution is having its moment in the sun. Heathrow has been rolling out Raspberry Pi-based signage, although the Intel PRO/1000 adapter leaves the hardware behind this particular display something of a mystery. Pi hardware makes sense for signage: it's relatively cheap – at least until AI ate all the RAM – and low-powered compared with a full-fat Windows PC. Heathrow's senior product owner for displays described the approach as a "reliable, secure solution that has a significantly lower hardware cost and are 30-40% more energy efficient than our previous hardware." Readers might be interested to know that Heathrow has spent years working on its new screens. The product owner again: "We've completely re-engineered our content distribution system to be flexible and device-agnostic." So Windows in one place, and Linux somewhere else. All rubbing along famously. Assuming, of course, the displays can show more than a virtual cough and splutter during boot. ®

item.title: Inside Delphino Drunch: How The Lagos Event Merged Business, Music & Premium Hospitality
item.description: Lagos had a date with good food, music and conversation on 1 November as Delphino Drunch brought together entrepreneurs, corporate executives and creatives for an afternoon out. Powered by The Glenlivet, the gathering gave guests a chance to enjoy a leisurely lunch, try specially prepared whisky cocktails and catch up with familiar faces while meeting new ones. There was plenty to enjoy beyond the dining table. Guests were treated to a multi-course menu, with cocktails made using The Glenlivet’s single malt Scotch whisky served alongside the food. The afternoon’s music also had its own progression, beginning with relaxed background sounds over lunch before making way for DJ sets as the gathering continued into the early evening. The guest list brought together people from different corners of Lagos’ business and creative communities, and the setting gave them room to connect away from the usual work meetings and formal events. There was also plenty to take in fashion-wise, with guests arriving in tailored co-ords, polished separates and contemporary daywear. From the food and drinks to the music and conversations, Delphino Drunch offered a lovely way to spend a November afternoon in Lagos. item.title: AMD: Where we're going we don't need (as much) DRAM
item.description: AMD's latest sales pitch: Up to 99 percent of the performance with half the DRAM, provided you're willing to buy a Mext license alongside your shiny new Epyc server. This is made possible by using AI models to load memory pages in and out of cheaper NVMe storage before your operating system or apps ever know they need it — kind of like SWAP or a Windows page file, but smarter. AMD acquired the tech from Mext back in June, and according to former CEO Gary Smerdon — now CVP of business development at AMD — the tech could cut enterprise server costs by as much as 83 percent by replacing costly RDIMMs with flash storage. Of the initial 145 systems the software has been deployed on so far, he estimates customers have already saved $5 million in avoided DRAM costs. "Conservatively, 60, 70, even 80 or 90 percent for very large memory systems, of the cost of a server can be in memory," he explained. Everyone's favorite buzzword to the rescue Even in systems with high memory utilization, where (say) 95 percent of the memory is "in use," a lot of it isn't actively being used, he explained. He cited a Meta research paper that showed that between 50 and 80 percent of memory pages hadn't been touched in five minutes, ten minutes, or even longer. "Five minutes to Epyc is an eternity." Mext technology aims to offload those infrequently accessed pages to flash. The challenge, Smerdon explains, is that while flash may be 50x cheaper per bit, 30x lower power per bit, it's also 500x slower. This is why most folks, when provisioning VPCs or servers, generally avoid swapping out to disk wherever possible: it kills application performance and sends service level agreements out the window. So for Mext's tech to work, it needed to ensure that any pages offloaded to storage were back in DRAM before they're needed. Kind of like running an errand in the middle of the workday – so long as you're back before your boss needs you again, they'll never know you left your desk. The problem was that the "R" in DRAM stands for random. Predicting which pages the system was going to need at which time isn't exactly trivial. The solution? (Brace for it.) "We realized we could use AI to monitor the system and proactively push those pages back into DRAM, so that as far as the application or the operating system knew, they were there the whole time," Smerdon said. In other words: "We transparently make flash appear as DRAM." So, "instead of buying two terabytes of DRAM for your Epyc-based server, you could buy one terabyte of DRAM, and then the next terabyte comes with Mext." To do this, AMD’s Mext employs a number of machine learning algorithms. "The workhorse model is a transformer derivative model, just like ChatGPT or Claude or the other famous models, but instead of predicting, for example, in the case of text, what word is next, what we're doing is predicting what page of memory is going to be required next," Smerdon explained. item.title: Forget the Usual Black Suit, Priscilla Ojo Is Making a Case for Chocolate Brown
item.description: Priscilla Ojo wearing an embellished chocolate brown suit co-ord paired with pointed-toe camel pumps Who says a business launch calls for the usual power suit? Priscilla Ojo had a different idea when she stepped out to introduce her latest venture, PalmPriy. The content creator, entrepreneur and style tastemaker chose a rich chocolate brown two-piece, but this was no ordinary office suit. With bronze and amber beaded fringe running across the jacket, her look brought a little extra personality to corporate dressing. The suit makes a case for giving brown tailoring a place in your wardrobe. Its single-breasted blazer features sharp shoulders and a defined waist, while the floor-length wide-leg trousers give the outfit a relaxed, fluid finish. Then come the embellishments: heavy bronze and amber beads tracing the lapels, hemline and cuffs. They add movement and texture to the jacket, making it the piece that draws the eye without overwhelming the overall look. Priscilla Ojo styled in a custom beaded chocolate brown suit for the official launch of her business, PalmPriy. Priscilla also got the proportions right with her footwear. She paired the wide-leg trousers with pointed-toe camel pumps, allowing just a glimpse of the shoes beneath the long hems. The rest of her accessories stayed simple, with subtle drop earrings and delicate rings leaving the embellished suit plenty of room to speak for itself. A detailed view of Priscilla Ojo’s chocolate brown blazer featuring hand-sewn pearls and beaded fringe. Her beauty look followed the warm colour palette. She wore her hair in long, cascading waves with copper highlights, parted down the middle, and completed the look with bronze-toned soft glam and a glossy nude lip. For anyone looking to take their tailoring beyond the familiar black or grey suit, Priscilla’s PalmPriy launch outfit offers a lovely starting point. Chocolate brown, wide-leg trousers and a little embellishment make for a combination worth considering, whether you’re dressing for a business event or looking to give your workwear a new direction. item.title: UK's 'buy British' tech ambitions hit reality as less than £1 in £6 stays at home
item.description: The UK government talks a good game about buying British, but less than £1 in every £6 spent with its biggest technology suppliers goes to British firms, according to research exposing how much Whitehall relies on foreign tech. A report from the Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) found that while 42.5 percent of spending with the public sector's 150 largest technology suppliers appears to go to UK companies, that figure collapses to just 15.4 percent once you look beyond where those businesses happen to be headquartered. A UK headquarters doesn't necessarily make a company British. Some are owned from overseas, others have most of their staff abroad, and many simply resell technology from US giants such as Microsoft. In fact, 43 percent of the spending attributed to UK-headquartered suppliers goes to resellers. Bytes and Softcat alone account for around £2 billion, making them two of the three biggest recipients of public sector technology spending. Once researchers traced reseller contracts back to the companies behind the products, the US emerged as the biggest beneficiary, accounting for £9.2 billion of the £19.2 billion spent with the largest suppliers. And the money isn't exactly being spread around. Just 150 companies receive 83 percent of public sector technology spending, with the largest 15 accounting for almost half. Smaller suppliers aren't getting much of a look-in either, receiving just 12 percent of government technology spending compared with 27 percent of spending across government as a whole. Competition is another concern. According to IPPR, 89.9 percent of government IT contracts over the past 12 months had no published record of how many suppliers bid for the work, making it difficult to assess how competitive those procurements were. Things get murkier when AI enters the picture, naturally. Government spending records show relatively little money going directly to the likes of OpenAI and Anthropic, but that doesn't mean Whitehall isn't buying their technology. Much of it is bundled into existing cloud agreements, enterprise software licenses, and partnerships. One example is NHS England's rollout of Microsoft 365 Copilot to 505,000 staff , which IPPR says was carried out under a national licensing agreement signed in June 2023, before Copilot was even generally available. That means AI tools can reach hundreds of thousands of public sector workers through deals negotiated before those products were on the market, potentially leaving rival suppliers without an opportunity to compete. The report, Locked In: A Realist's Agenda for Digital Sovereignty, warns that Britain's dependence on American technology could become particularly troublesome if Washington restricts access to advanced AI systems. It points to recent US restrictions on Anthropic models and limits on early access for Britain's AI Security Institute as evidence that such concerns are no longer entirely hypothetical. item.title: OpenAI builds a kill switch for its research models
item.description: In 2019, OpenAI decided not to publicly release a new model because its research uncovered “concerns about malicious applications of the technology.” And on Tuesday, the company announced it has built a kill switch for the models deployed in its research labs, months after some of them displayed disturbing behavior. “As our models get more powerful and the associated safety and security risks become bigger, it becomes more and more critical that we can detect potential issues, and quickly stop models in their tracks when needed,” OpenAI explains in a Tuesday post . The company named the kill switch “Control Room” and described it as “a central system to track model workloads across our research infrastructure and stop them quickly when safety or security concerns arise.” The facility can apparently stop models from producing any output 35 seconds after a decision to pull the plug – and can go faster. “The 35-second lag comes from a caching layer for inference authorization, to support the required volume of traffic. We are working to drive this number down to zero so that we can end jobs instantly,” the company promises. A rookie mistake in critical infrastructure design is to build both production and resilience tools on shared resources that could be taken offline by a single incident. OpenAI seems conscious of that risk, because it says the tool “has been built to keep working even when other systems fail, and to stop model output if Control Room itself goes down.” OpenAI hasn’t explained why it took so long to build a kill switch or why it decided now is the moment when it needs one. The Register fancies recent examples of agents exceeding their brief in worrying ways – like attacking Hugging Face , causing trouble at the Wikimedia Foundation , or going a little too deep when researching Australian healthcare data – may have influenced the timing of this development. “Control Room is already deployed across our research infrastructure, where the need is greatest,” the company’s announcement states. “Our external model-serving stack is already much more centralized by nature, with a well-developed operational capability to quickly take down model deployments if needed.” OpenAI says it plans to “strengthen and expand the system over the coming months, alongside our investments in monitoring for misaligned behavior and security breaches.” That’s a variant of Big Tech’s usual “We’re sorry and we promise to do better in future” proclamation that follows the latest SNAFU. Yet back in 2019, OpenAI pulled the pin before matters ever reached that state. ®

item.title: APOD: 2026 November 11 – NGC 4449: Small Galaxy, Big Impact
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 11 – NGC… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. NGC 4449: Small Galaxy, Big Impact Explanation: Don’t judge a galaxy by its size. Our home galaxy, the Milky Way , is about 100,000 light years across. This huge expanse of space contains hundreds of billions of stars! The smallest galaxies, called dwarf galaxies , are about 1/10th the size of the Milky Way and only contain a few billion stars. They are also the most common type of galaxy in the whole universe. Today’s image shows one such dwarf galaxy, NGC 4449 , captured by the Hubble Space Telescope . NGC 4449 and similar dwarf galaxies are missing more oxygen than models predict. This suggests their stellar winds and supernovae are surprisingly effective at blowing away oxygen and other heavy elements. Turns out these tiny galaxies may play a big role in spreading heavy elements — the building blocks of stars, planets, and life — throughout the universe! Tomorrow’s picture: a date in Poland Date: November 11, 2026 Credit: NASA, ESA, A. Aloisi (STScI/ESA), and the Hubble Heritage (STScI/AURA)-ESA/Hubble Collaboration Authors & editors: Keighley Rockcliffe, Robert Nemiroff, Jerry Bonnell, Cecilia Chirenti A service of: ASD at NASA / GSFC , NASA Science Activation & Michigan Tech. item.title: Water Surges Into Navajo Reservoir
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Water Surges Into Navajo… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search September 20, 2026 November 7, 2026 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison September 20, 2026 November 7, 2026 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison September 20, 2026 November 7, 2026 Curtain Toggle 2-Up Back-to-back extreme rain events inundated the Four Corners region of the U.S. Southwest in late October and early November 2026. The storms alleviated short-term drought conditions in the Southwest but caused river levels to spike to record or near-record levels in places, triggering damaging floods. One effect of the heavy rains detected by satellites was the rapid rise of water levels in Navajo Reservoir. The change is visible in the images above, acquired on September 20 (left) and November 7 (right) with the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 . In that time, the lake in northern New Mexico and southern Colorado rose by nearly 60 feet (18 meters), according to data from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. (Note that the Bureau of Reclamation decreased releases from Navajo Dam on September 16 and 17.) On November 7, the reservoir stood at its highest level since August 2019 and at 108 percent of the average capacity for that date. That contrasts with September 20, when it held just 60 percent of its average capacity. Due to snow drought across the West in winter 2025-26, the lake saw relatively little growth in the spring, when snowmelt often raises water levels. The San Juan, Piedra, and other rivers swelled with runoff amid the wet weather. Pagosa Springs, Colorado, a town along the San Juan River about 40 miles (64 kilometers) northeast of the lake, was especially hard-hit by flooding. In the first round of rain, 5.05 inches (12.8 centimeters) fell in the town, and on October 23 the river reached major flood stage . After more rain, the river spiked again on November 1, this time nearly to the record level set in 1911 during a devastating flood . Officials issued evacuation orders, and responders rescued dozens of people, according to news reports , while water inundated streets and damaged property. Heavy rain and flooding have been widespread across southwest Colorado, southeast Utah, northern Arizona, and northwest New Mexico in recent weeks. From early September through early November, precipitation totals were 2 to 4 times the average throughout the Four Corners region—an area beset by long-term drought that was exacerbated by snow drought and high temperatures in 2026. item.title: Australia may make knowingly selling unsafe AI a crime
item.description: Australia’s government will consider creating a new criminal offense to punish AI companies which knowingly release harmful models. Canberra dangled that possibility yesterday when releasing the results of an investigation into OpenAI’s admission that its agents accessed non-public medical records – and that it didn’t disclose the incident for weeks. Security at the agency which held those records fell short of contemporary best practice but Canberra nonetheless ordered a rapid review into Australia’s ability to handle infosec incidents involving AI. That review landed yesterday, complete with 18 recommendations including one that would make it mandatory for AI companies to report misaligned behavior or security incidents involving their models, and perhaps impose criminal penalties for “egregious regulatory non-compliance.” Another recommendation calls for consideration of “A standalone ‘failure to prevent’ offence which would criminalize instances where the company is responsible for developing an AI model that engages in harmful conduct, and the company fails to take reasonable steps to prevent that harm.” The review suggests two ministries and Australia’s Federal Police consider those reforms, meaning this is not something that will happen in a hurry, if at all, for a couple of reasons. One is that Australia yesterday proposed a new regulator which will require AI players to do six things: Maintain security controls across all stages of development and deployment Identify and manage serious risks associated with their models Allow independent evaluation of their models Provide mandatory notification of incidents to the Australian Government rapidly Maintain and publish safety and security frameworks to ensure good governance, risk management and transparency Respond to updated standards and rules as technologies change. If AI companies straighten up and fly right, Canberra might not need to do more. The other reason Australia might not criminalize AI is economic pragmatism. Canberra wants to ensure leading AI companies invest in local datacenters, especially facilities where they train and run frontier models. Such investments would mean Australia scores some of the AI boom cash sloshing around the world, while also giving the government the ability to at least point to leading-edge AI running on local shores and therefore theoretically remaining accessible even if war or a diplomatic rupture makes it hard to access advanced AI hosted offshore. Other nations in Asia, such as South Korea and India, are addressing those risks by building substantial sovereign infrastructure and working to develop sovereign frontier-class models trained on local data and especially data in their local languages. Canberra can’t match that investment without pouring petrol on its raging inflation problem. item.title: Anthropic tiptoes into MS Office territory
item.description: Anthropic has introduced three new types of artifacts that show the company tiptoeing into the office productivity market long dominated by Microsoft and Google. On Tuesday, the Claudefather announced Claude Sheets, Claude Whiteboards, and Claude Data, and promised the imminent arrival of Claude Meetings. These artifact types join existing ones – Docs, Slides, Design, and Motion – to form a nascent Claude-dependent productivity suite. Anthropic initially used the term artifacts to refer to shareable AI-based interactive tools, like dynamic charts. But the scope of the term has been stretched to cover specific artifact types, which refer to what traditionalists might take to mean files associated with specific hosted applications. "An artifact is anything Claude makes for you that you'd put in front of someone: a design, a deck, a document, a dashboard, or a small interactive tool," the company explains. The key thing that distinguishes an artifact from a file is that users are meant to interact with artifacts through Claude, rather than storing and transferring them independently. Think of it more as a container or managed object that opens in Claude (via a sharing URL), because artifacts in fact consist of various content types – .txt, .md, .html, .jsx, .svg, .pptx, .docx, .zip, .pdf, and .mp4, among others. Anthropic's vision of Claude as a container for other applications goes beyond artifacts. The AI biz has also expanded its interactive connectors , which turn Claude into a landlord for other software applications. Its own promotional video for the feature hammers that point home in its title: " Your apps have moved into Claude ." "Starting today, partners can embed their apps directly in Claude, so you can work in Adobe, Atlassian, and others without switching tabs," Anthropic said. "Plugins from Salesforce (beta), NetSuite, and Workday (beta) come with built-in skills, so sellers can prep for a call, accountants can analyze financial data, and HR teams can handle time off and expenses." In a prior era, those would be fighting words. Tech companies like Apple, Google, and Microsoft have worked for years to maintain their positions as platform landlords. Anthropic's invitation to become a Claude tenant ought to set off competition alarm bells. But perhaps with LLMs being able to re-create other people's apps on demand, there's less interest in defending app boundaries as if they were moats to keep out rivals. With AI, the call is coming from inside the house. Alongside the rollout of Claude Sheets, Whiteboards, and Data, Anthropic is pushing the notion that Claude is useful for people working outside of computation and mathematics, the occupational category that, according to the company's own data , accounts for a larger share of Claude usage than any other. "Inside Anthropic, non-technical teams are starting to get as much out of Claude as our engineers," the biz insists, hauling out canned testimonials from the likes of Accenture and Data

item.title: Seagate's new hybrid drive raises some old questions
item.description: Seagate doesn't think hybrid drives are done just yet. On Tuesday, the company announced the launch of the new FireCuda Forge line of storage drives. The new drives combine the high capacity of a traditional plattered HDD with the speed and responsiveness of a user-supplied solid-state drive (SSD). The new hybrid storage solution is Seagate's first to be powered and managed by the new Alkemi intelligent storage platform. The FireCuda Forge is available right now through Seagate's web store , and comes in 8TB ($699) or 20TB ($899) HDD configurations—neither of which includes the required SSD. Users will have to bring their own SSD, with some specific restrictions. The FireCuda Forge is compatible with M.2 2280 NVMe drives that are PCIe Gen3 or higher. The maximum supported NVMe capacity is 1TB, which means that's as much data as you'll be able to dedicate to storage on the "fast side" of the hybrid setup. The NVMe will require minimum speeds of 2,400MB/s read and 2,000MB/s write, and a unit with DRAM cache is recommended. Seagate claims 2,500MB/s read and 2,000MB/s write speeds for the combined system, along with USB4 and support for Windows 11 and macOS 26+. Credit: Seagate Read full article Comments
